The orlistat result is reported in the prescription product’s clinical evidence. Different populations, durations and outcome definitions mean the rows cannot give a reliable personal “extra weight I will lose” calculation. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-4" aria-label="Source 4: SURMOUNT-1 trial">[4]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: Xenical pooled clinical evidence">[2]</a></p><p>The injection evidence makes substantial average weight reduction a legitimate topic for assessment. It does not make a tablet automatically pointless, nor does avoiding injections make orlistat risk-free. Ask which outcome is realistic for your circumstances and how it will be reviewed.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="meals"><span id="heading-meals">Orlistat changes the meal-time calculation</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>For prescription Xenical, the capsule is taken immediately before, during or up to one hour after a main meal. A dose is omitted when a meal is missed or contains no fat. Higher-fat meals can make gastrointestinal effects more troublesome. Follow your own product’s instructions rather than applying this automatically to another strength. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: Xenical administration instructions">[2]</a></p><p>Think about a working day: do you eat regular meals, can you access a toilet easily, and would you understand when a dose is not needed? Discuss how to maintain balanced nutrition rather than responding by skipping food or eliminating fat altogether.</p><p>Orlistat can affect fat-soluble vitamin absorption and interact with other medicines. Ask the pharmacist to check your full medication and supplement list, and whether vitamin advice is needed. NHS information distinguishes prescription Xenical from lower-dose products such as Alli and Orlos. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-3" aria-label="Source 3: NHS orlistat precautions and products">[3]</a></p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="safety"><span id="heading-safety">Side effects: different does not mean trivial</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>For Mounjaro, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea are recognised adverse effects. Other diabetes treatments may also need review. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: Mounjaro precautions">[1]</a></p><p><strong>Do not dismiss severe, persistent abdominal pain as an ordinary side effect.</strong> Pain that may spread to your back, with or without vomiting, needs urgent medical assessment because pancreatitis is a possible serious reaction to these injections. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-5" aria-label="Source 5: MHRA pancreatitis warning">[5]</a></p><p>For either treatment, contact your treating service when symptoms are persistent, severe or prevent normal eating and drinking. Do not assume that an unpleasant reaction proves the medicine is working. Read the patient leaflet supplied with the exact product.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="review"><span id="heading-review">Agree the review and stopping plan before you start</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Prescription orlistat should be discontinued if at least 5% of initial body weight has not been lost after 12 weeks. That is a clinical review point, not a reason to take additional capsules. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: Xenical stopping rule">[2]</a></p><p>For the injection, ask when benefit and tolerability will be reviewed and what would justify continuing. Compare the full ongoing cost—including clinical support—not just the medicine’s introductory price. Keep a plan for interruptions and stopping, rather than assuming that a short course resolves everything permanently.</p><p>Do not add orlistat to an injection or switch products on the basis of this page. The MHRA advises discussing GLP-1 switches with a healthcare professional. Your existing prescription and other medicines belong in that conversation. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-6" aria-label="Source 6: MHRA switching advice">[6]</a></p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="questions"><span id="heading-questions">A better decision than “jabs or tablets?”</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li>What does my medical history rule in or out?</li><li>Can I follow this routine during an ordinary working week?</li><li>Which side effects would require a call, a review or urgent help?</li><li>What would count as enough benefit, and when will we decide?</li><li>What support continues if the medicine changes or stops?</li></ul></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="guide-programme-cta-v30c"><span id="heading-guide-programme-cta-v30c">Keep the everyday plan with you</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The Programme and My Timber provide a place for food, movement, goals and your own treatment history. A saved entry is a personal record—not a verified prescription or an instruction to change medicine.</p><p><a href="/programme">See the Programme</a> · <a href="/member/dashboard?passport=1#journey">Keep your history in My Timber</a> · <a href="/guides/nhs-weight-loss-medication-pathways">Understand NHS access</a></p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="faq" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="fa-faq-heading">Common questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>Is Mounjaro better than orlistat?</h3><p>The studies above do not provide a direct head-to-head comparison of these medicines. The tirzepatide result is a percentage reduction from starting weight; the orlistat figure is additional kilograms lost compared with placebo. They cannot be used to calculate your personal advantage from one medicine. Discuss expected benefit alongside side effects, day-to-day use and the review or stopping plan with your prescriber. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1">[1]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2">[2]</a></p><h3>Is orlistat safer than Mounjaro?</h3><p>Safety depends on your medical history, other medicines and tolerability. Mounjaro and orlistat have different side effects and precautions, so a capsule-versus-injection label cannot decide which is appropriate for you. Ask your prescriber to assess your circumstances and explain the warning signs and review plan. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1">[1]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2">[2]</a></p><h3>Is orlistat a tablet version of Mounjaro?</h3><p>No. The medicines have different mechanisms and routines. Orlistat acts on fat absorption in the gut; tirzepatide acts on GIP/<a href="/glp1-knowledge-centre" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">GLP-1</a> receptors.</p><h3>Does “3.2 kg” mean that is all someone loses on orlistat?</h3><p>No. The cited pooled result is the mean additional loss compared with placebo after one year. It is not a total weight-loss forecast.</p><h3>Can I take both together?</h3><p>This comparison does not establish that a combination is appropriate or safe for you. Do not combine or switch them without the prescribing team assessing your treatment.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="sources" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="fa-sources-heading">Sources and editorial responsibility</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ol><li id="source-1"><a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15481/smpc">Mounjaro: UK summary of product characteristics</a></li><li id="source-2"><a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/2592/smpc">Xenical 120 mg: UK summary of product characteristics</a></li><li id="source-3"><a href="https://www.nhs.uk/medicines/orlistat/">NHS: orlistat—uses, side effects and precautions</a></li><li id="source-4"><a href="https://www.nejm.org/doi/abs/10.1056/NEJMoa2206038">Jastreboff et al., SURMOUNT-1, New England Journal of Medicine (2022)</a></li><li id="source-5"><a href="https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases">MHRA: strengthened warnings on acute pancreatitis, 29 January 2026</a></li><li id="source-6"><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know">MHRA: GLP-1 medicines—what you need to know</a></li></ol><p>Product information and access arrangements can change. General information, not individual medical advice.</p><p class="fa-lead"><a href="/mounjaro" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Mounjaro</a> is a weekly injection; Saxenda is a daily injection. Tirzepatide produced larger average weight losses in the separate trials summarised below, but those studies did not compare it directly with liraglutide. The useful question is which option is appropriate, tolerable and sustainable for you—not which one wins an invented score out of ten.</p><p>This guide compares their adult weight-management use in the UK. It does not select a medicine or dose for you. Clinical suitability, NHS funding and whether a pharmacy can supply a prescription are three separate questions.</p></div><div class="qr-graphic rest-art" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true"><p id="at-a-glance"><span id="heading-at-a-glance">What actually differs?</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table><caption>Adult weight-management medicines: practical comparison</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Question</th><th scope="col">Mounjaro</th><th scope="col">Saxenda</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Active ingredient</th><td>Tirzepatide</td><td>Liraglutide</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">How it works</th><td>Acts on GIP and GLP-1 receptors</td><td>Acts on GLP-1 receptors</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Routine</th><td>Once-weekly injection</td><td>Once-daily injection</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Licensed adult weight-management starting criteria</th><td>BMI at least 30, or at least 27 with a weight-related condition</td><td>BMI at least 30, or at least 27 with a weight-related condition</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">A useful review question</th><td>What benefit, side effects and review plan justify continuing?</td><td>Has the adult stopping rule been assessed after 12 weeks on the 3.0 mg daily dose?</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>These are product-licence details, not a promise of NHS eligibility. Both require prescribing assessment and are used alongside changes to eating and activity. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: Mounjaro UK product information">[1]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: Saxenda UK product information">[2]</a></p></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="trial-evidence"><span id="heading-trial-evidence">What do the weight-loss studies really show?</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Compare the study design before comparing the headline. Both trials below enrolled adults without diabetes and included lifestyle support. Neither was a men-only trial. Their durations, participants and doses differed.</p><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table><caption>Separate placebo-controlled trials—not a head-to-head comparison</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Study</th><th scope="col">Treatment and duration</th><th scope="col">Average body-weight reduction</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">SURMOUNT-1; 2,539 adults</th><td>Tirzepatide 5, 10 or 15 mg weekly; 72 weeks</td><td>15.0%, 19.5% and 20.9%, respectively; placebo 3.1%</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">SCALE Obesity and Prediabetes; 3,731 adults</th><td>Liraglutide 3.0 mg daily; 56 weeks</td><td>8.0%; placebo 2.6%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>Sources: original trial publications. SURMOUNT-1 was funded by Eli Lilly; SCALE by Novo Nordisk. These are average study outcomes, not guaranteed results or starting-dose effects. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-3" aria-label="Source 3: SURMOUNT-1 trial">[3]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-4" aria-label="Source 4: SCALE trial">[4]</a></p><p><strong>What you can reasonably take away:</strong> the tirzepatide results support a discussion about substantial weight reduction. What you cannot do is subtract these two trials and claim that a particular man will lose that much more after switching. A Mounjaro-versus-Wegovy trial would not answer the Mounjaro-versus-Saxenda question either.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="daily-life"><span id="heading-daily-life">Which routine is more workable for your life?</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Put the prescription into an ordinary week. Would a daily injection be easier to attach to a routine, or would a weekly appointment with yourself be easier to remember? Who will answer questions when you feel unwell? How will you handle travel, sharps disposal and obtaining the next supply?</p><p>Ask for the total ongoing cost at the anticipated maintenance dose, including consultations, delivery and any separately charged support. A cheap first month does not tell you whether the next six months fit your budget. Ask what happens if treatment is interrupted; do not plan a restart from the dose on an old box.</p><p>Agree what success means beyond a smaller number: improved day-to-day function, a plan you can maintain, and side effects you can manage. Record questions and symptoms for your prescriber rather than treating a comparison table as a treatment plan.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="safety"><span id="heading-safety">Side effects and the point at which you need help</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea are recognised effects of these medicines; tolerability matters as well as effectiveness. Tell the prescriber about other medicines, particularly insulin or sulfonylureas, and any relevant digestive or pancreatic history. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: Mounjaro UK product information">[1]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: Saxenda UK product information">[2]</a></p><p><strong>Do not dismiss severe, persistent abdominal pain as an ordinary side effect.</strong> Pain that may spread to your back, with or without vomiting, needs urgent medical assessment because pancreatitis is a possible serious reaction to these injections. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-5" aria-label="Source 5: MHRA pancreatitis warning">[5]</a></p><p>Contact your treating service promptly when symptoms interfere with eating, drinking or ordinary activity. Severe symptoms, collapse or an immediate threat to life require emergency help. Do not increase a dose to compensate for a disappointing week on the scales.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="switching"><span id="heading-switching">Switching is a clinical handover—not a dose conversion</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Speak to the prescribing team before changing medicine or brand. The MHRA specifically advises discussing a switch with a healthcare professional. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-6">[6]</a></p><p><strong>Before discussing a switch from Saxenda to Mounjaro, have these details ready:</strong></p><ul><li>The exact product and dose you currently use.</li><li>The date of your last injection.</li><li>Any side effects and treatment gaps.</li></ul><p><strong>Ask the prescribing team for written instructions covering:</strong></p><ul><li>The last dose of the old medicine and the first dose of the new one.</li><li>Who owns the follow-up.</li><li>What to do if you cannot tolerate the new treatment.</li></ul><p>Do not combine these injections or invent a milligram-for-milligram conversion yourself.</p><p>For adults using Saxenda, its product information says to discontinue if at least 5% of initial body weight has not been lost after <strong>12 weeks at 3.0 mg a day</strong>. That is not simply 12 weeks after the first starter dose. Your clinician should assess the stopping rule and alternatives. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: Saxenda adult stopping rule">[2]</a></p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="questions"><span id="heading-questions">Take these questions to the prescriber</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li>What makes this medicine appropriate for my medical history and goals?</li><li>What is the review point, and what would lead us to continue, change or stop?</li><li>What is the complete ongoing cost, and who handles side effects or supply interruptions?</li><li>Can I leave with a written handover plan rather than infer one from the internet?</li></ul></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="guide-programme-cta-v30c"><span id="heading-guide-programme-cta-v30c">Keep the support separate from the prescription</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>SHIFT’s Programme brings together food, movement and everyday support; My Timber can keep your own goals and treatment history in one place. Those records are not a prescription or a clinician’s approval. Use them to make the next conversation easier.</p><p><a href="/programme">Explore the Programme</a> · <a href="/member/dashboard?passport=1#journey">Open your Health Passport in My Timber</a> · <a href="/guides/nhs-weight-loss-medication-pathways">Check the separate NHS access routes</a></p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="faq" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="fa-faq-heading">Common questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>Is Mounjaro better than Saxenda?</h3><p>Separate trials reported greater average weight reduction with tirzepatide, but this page does not present a direct comparison trial or a personalised prediction. Suitability, adverse effects, support and affordability still matter.</p><h3>Can I switch straight from Saxenda to Mounjaro?</h3><p>A prescriber needs to plan the change using your current treatment, last dose, treatment gaps and tolerability. Do not overlap medicines or calculate a replacement dose yourself.</p><h3>Does meeting the licence criteria mean I can get it on the NHS?</h3><p>No. NHS commissioning, referral and prioritisation rules are distinct from a medicine’s licence. See the NHS pathways guide and check your local service.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="sources" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="fa-sources-heading">Sources and editorial responsibility</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ol><li id="source-1"><a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15481/smpc">Mounjaro: UK summary of product characteristics</a></li><li id="source-2"><a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/2313/smpc">Saxenda: UK summary of product characteristics</a></li><li id="source-3"><a href="https://www.nejm.org/doi/abs/10.1056/NEJMoa2206038">Jastreboff et al., SURMOUNT-1, New England Journal of Medicine (2022)</a></li><li id="source-4"><a href="https://www.nejm.org/doi/abs/10.1056/NEJMoa1411892">Pi-Sunyer et al., SCALE, New England Journal of Medicine (2015)</a></li><li id="source-5"><a href="https://www.gov.uk/drug-safety-update/glp-1-receptor-agonists-and-dual-glp-1-slash-gip-receptor-agonists-strengthened-warnings-on-acute-pancreatitis-including-necrotising-and-fatal-cases">MHRA: strengthened warnings on acute pancreatitis, 29 January 2026</a></li><li id="source-6"><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know/glp-1-medicines-for-weight-loss-and-diabetes-what-you-need-to-know">MHRA: GLP-1 medicines—what you need to know</a></li></ol><p>Product information and access arrangements can change. <div><h2>Reasons to discuss Wegovy injection</h2><ul><li>Large evidence base</li><li>Weekly dosing</li><li>Cardiovascular outcome evidence in appropriate populations</li><li>2.4 mg established; 7.2 mg injectable option now licensed for adults with obesity if needed</li></ul><h3>Trade-offs</h3><ul><li>Injection</li><li>GI effects</li><li>The new 7.2 mg option should not be compared using old 2.4 mg-only trial assumptions</li><li>NHS access remains pathway-limited</li></ul></div></div></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-comparisons--medications--ozempic-vs-wegovy-2">How should I compare weight-loss evidence?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Read the named evidence above with its population, duration and outcome measure. mechanism</li><li>Can be appropriate where other options are unsuitable</li><li>Licensed specifically for weight management</li></ul><h3>Trade-offs</h3><ul><li>Daily injection</li><li>Lower average weight loss than newer weekly incretin treatments</li><li>NHS use is restricted</li><li>Daily adherence burden</li></ul></div>
<div><h2>Reasons to discuss Orlistat</h2><ul><li>Needle-free</li><li>Generic and established</li><li>Different mechanism from incretin medicines</li><li>Usually lower drug cost than branded incretin therapy</li></ul><h3>Trade-offs</h3><ul><li>Lower average efficacy</li><li>Oily stools/urgency and other GI effects can be disruptive</li><li>Must be taken around fat-containing meals</li><li>Fat-soluble vitamin considerations</li></ul></div></div></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-comparisons--medications--saxenda-vs-orlistat-2">How should I compare weight-loss evidence?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Read the named evidence above with its population, duration and outcome measure. Separate-trial results cannot establish a direct treatment ranking or predict your result. Ask which evidence is relevant to your own circumstances.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-comparisons--medications--saxenda-vs-orlistat-3" data-section="03">Which is easier to live with?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Liraglutide (Saxenda / licensed equivalents): Once daily. Orlistat: Up to three times daily with fat-containing meals. Consider the actual formulation and frequency above, its administration instructions and how it fits your routine.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="can-you-take-saxenda-and-orlistat-together">Can you take Saxenda and Orlistat together?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><strong>Do not combine them on your own.</strong> Saxenda (liraglutide) and orlistat work differently, but that does not establish that taking both is safe or more effective. The <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/2313/smpc" rel="noopener noreferrer">UK Saxenda Summary of Product Characteristics</a> states that safety and efficacy have not been established in people treated with other products for weight management, and that use in these patients is not recommended.</p><p>If you already take either medicine, ask the prescriber responsible for your treatment before adding or switching anything. They need to consider your medical history, other medicines, possible adverse effects and the authorised indications. This page compares the two options; it is not a recommendation to use them together.</p><p>Sources checked 23 October 2026: UK Saxenda SmPC, section 4.4 (emc); <a href="https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246/chapter/Medicines-and-surgery" rel="noopener noreferrer">NICE NG246 medicines guidance</a>.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-comparisons--medications--saxenda-vs-orlistat-5" data-section="04">NHS vs private reality</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>NICE option in specialist services for defined groups; pathway availability varies. Long-established NHS option; prescribing criteria and local practice apply. NICE criteria and NHS availability are related but not identical, so check the current pathway rather than assuming a clinically eligible medicine is immediately available through a GP.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-comparisons--medications--saxenda-vs-orlistat-6" data-section="05">Maintenance matters</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Ongoing treatment and maintenance strategy matter. data-practical-guide="tablets-and-injections-uk" id="tablets-and-injections-uk"><h2>Tablets or injections: what changes in everyday life?</h2>
<p><strong>A daily tablet can remove the needle, but it adds a daily task.</strong> The right option depends on an individual clinical assessment, your other medicines, tolerability, cost and a routine you can manage.</p>
<div class="shift-practical-table" role="region" aria-label="Tablet and injection routine comparison" tabindex="0"><table><caption>Practical differences to discuss with your prescriber</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">Routine</th><th scope="col">Useful question</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Wegovy tablets — semaglutide</th><td>Every day. At least eight hours fasting; swallow whole with a sip of water, up to 120 mL. Wait at least 30 minutes before food, drink or other oral medicines.</td><td>Can I manage the fasting window around breakfast, coffee, shifts and my other tablets?</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Foundayo tablets — orforglipron</th><td>Every day, at any time, with or without food. No fasting or water timing restriction; swallow whole.</td><td>Which daily anchor fits my week, and do my other medicines need checking?</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Weekly injections, including Wegovy</th><td>A weekly injection with product-specific instructions for use, storage and missed doses.</td><td>Would a weekly task be easier to maintain, and am I comfortable using the pen?</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<h3>Are the tablets approved in the UK?</h3><p>MHRA authorised Wegovy tablets on 11 June 2026 and Foundayo on 10 August 2026. For weight management, both approvals cover adults with a BMI of at least 30, or at least 27 with a weight-related health condition, alongside diet and activity. Meeting that threshold does not establish that a medicine is suitable for you. A prescription and individual assessment are required.</p>
<p>UK authorisation is separate from NHS funding, a provider offering treatment and stock at your prescribed strength. These sources do not confirm a particular provider’s current supply. Read <a href="/articles/nhs-weight-loss-drugs">the NHS access guide</a> and ask your prescribing service to confirm availability before relying on an offer.</p>
<h3>Which gives better results or fewer side effects?</h3><p>A headline percentage from one trial cannot rank tablets against injections or another pill. Check the population, dose, duration, comparator, dropouts and how missing data were handled. Trial averages are not personal forecasts. The <a href="/articles/oral-semaglutide-for-weight-loss">oral-semaglutide evidence guide</a> explains the Wegovy tablet result in context; <a href="/foundayo">the Foundayo guide</a> covers that different medicine. A tablet does not remove gastrointestinal or other medicine risks.</p>
<h3>Can I switch from an injection?</h3><p>Ask the prescribing service for a written plan: the last dose of the current medicine, when the next medicine starts, the prescribed strength and the review date. Do not calculate a tablet dose from an injection dose, overlap medicines or restart after a break on your own. Wegovy tablets and Rybelsus are different licensed products and should not be treated as interchangeable.</p>
<h3>What will it cost after the introductory month?</h3><p>Ask for a written quote for the prescribed dose in month one and the anticipated dose in month four. Include the number of tablets or treatment days, consultation and review fees, delivery, ongoing support, cancellation terms and what happens if treatment is unsuitable or stock is unavailable. Compare equal treatment periods; a starting price is not the ongoing cost.</p>
<p><a href="/articles/oral-semaglutide-for-weight-loss#tablet-first-month">Use the first-month tablet plan</a>, including missed doses, shift work and questions for your pharmacist.</p>
<p><a href="/member/dashboard?view=app#today">Open My Timber’s Today screen</a> and look for “Your tablet routine”. If these tablets have already been prescribed for you, optional health tracking lets you save a routine, return for a first-week check-in and say whether a practical step helped. You can use routine support when treatment was arranged elsewhere. Saving a check-in does not contact a clinician; nobody monitors it for symptoms. Medicine decisions stay with your prescribing service.</p><p>For everyday support, use <a href="/guides/nutrition-protein-calories-meal-planning">food and meal planning</a> and <a href="/mens-weight-management">manageable movement and starting steps</a>.</p><p>Sources: <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/first-glp-1-tablet-for-weight-loss-approved-in-the-uk">MHRA: Wegovy tablets authorised, 11 June 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-first-in-europe-to-authorise-orforglipron-for-weight-management-and-type-2-diabetes">MHRA: Foundayo authorised, 10 August 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102344/pil">UK Wegovy tablet leaflet, revised June 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102529/pil">UK Foundayo leaflet, revised August 2026</a>.</p><p class="shift-practical-note">Practical section added and its linked sources checked 6 October 2026 by the SHIFT editorial team. class="qr-sections"><div class="qr-block"><aside class="sst-answer-review" aria-label="Quick comparison answer"><h2>Wegovy or orlistat: what is the practical difference?</h2><p>Wegovy and orlistat work differently. Wegovy contains semaglutide and is injected once a week; it reduces hunger and increases fullness. Orlistat is taken with fat-containing main meals and reduces how much dietary fat is absorbed. Both can cause digestive side effects. <section class="future-section"><h2>What should actually influence a decision?</h2>
<div class="future-grid">
<div class="future-card"><h3>Can you use it now?</h3><p>An authorised medicine with a regulated supply chain has a practical advantage over a future treatment, even when a future trial percentage looks larger.</p></div>
<div class="future-card"><h3>Does the evidence fit you?</h3><p>Diabetes status, starting BMI, comorbidities, trial duration and analysis methods affect results.</p></div>
<div class="future-card"><h3>Will you stick with it?</h3><p>Weekly injection, monthly injection and daily tablet all create different real-life adherence trade-offs.</p></div>
</div></section>
<section class="future-section"><h2>Current vs future: don't miss the obvious</h2>
<p>Some visitors will be deciding whether to use a treatment available today or wait for something newer. That is why Mounjaro and Wegovy are included as benchmark options in the dropdown.</p>
<p>If your health needs treatment now, a future drug should not automatically delay an appropriate current option. If you're doing well already, there is equally no need to jump treatments simply because a new one arrives.</p>
</section>
<section class="future-section"><h2>Direct head-to-head studies matter more than internet scorecards</h2>
<p>Retatrutide has a dedicated Phase 3 comparison programme against tirzepatide. CagriSema already has direct-comparison results from REDEFINE 4. Read the <a href="/guides/cagrisema-uk-guide">CagriSema guide for the dated results and limitations</a>. Direct trials answer more specific questions than comparisons of unrelated study averages; neither establishes the best treatment for every individual.</p>
</section>
<div class="future-verdict"><h2>Shift Says</h2>
<p>The most exciting treatment on paper isn't automatically the best treatment in real life. The winner is the option that is safe for you, evidence-based, genuinely available, affordable enough to sustain and effective enough to improve your health.</p>
<p>Use the checker to understand the landscape. Use a qualified clinician to make the treatment decision.</p></div>
</div></div></section>

Its 2025 annual report said the programme was advancing to initiate Phase 3 trials in 2026. It is not a routine UK prescription treatment today.</p><p>This is important because early weight-loss numbers have been eye-catching, but the treatment still needs the kind of larger and longer studies that establish practical dosing, safety, durability and comparative effectiveness.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-2">What is Amycretin / Zenagamtide?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Amycretin is a <strong>single molecule</strong> designed to activate both GLP-1 and amylin receptors. That makes it conceptually different from CagriSema, which combines two separate active medicines — semaglutide plus cagrilintide.</p><div class="future-grid"><div class="future-card"><h3>GLP-1 activity</h3><p>Targets appetite, fullness and glucose-dependent insulin signalling.</p></div>
<div class="future-card"><h3>Amylin activity</h3><p>Adds another satiety pathway associated with reduced food intake.</p></div>
<div class="future-card"><h3>One molecule</h3><p>The two activities are engineered into one unimolecular treatment rather than delivered as a two-drug combination.</p></div></div><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="mechanism" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-3">Why combine GLP-1 and amylin?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>GLP-1 and amylin both contribute to meal-related satiety but through partly different biological pathways. The theory is that combining them could create stronger appetite regulation than either pathway alone while avoiding the complexity of administering separate medicines.</p><p>The clinical question is whether that theoretical elegance actually translates into enough extra benefit, acceptable tolerability and a useful maintenance strategy.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="oral" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-4">Could Amycretin be a pill as well as an injection?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>One of the most interesting features of the programme is that both <strong>oral and subcutaneous</strong> formulations have been investigated. Novo Nordisk has reported substantial weight reduction in early studies of both forms.</p><p>If an oral formulation survives Phase 3 and regulatory review, it could matter commercially because many people dislike injections. But convenience alone does not decide whether a treatment is superior — adherence, dosing rules, cost, tolerability and weight-loss durability all matter.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="evidence" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-5">What has the evidence shown so far?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Published Phase 1b/2a research reported substantial body-weight reductions with weekly subcutaneous amycretin over 36 weeks, with the highest studied dose producing average weight loss in the mid-20% range in the trial analysis. Earlier oral studies also showed rapid weight reduction over shorter treatment periods.</p><strong>Important:</strong><p>Small and medium early-phase trials can look spectacular. Phase 3 is where we learn whether the effect is reproducible in larger, more diverse populations over longer periods.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="phase3" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-6">What happens in Phase 3?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Novo Nordisk moved zenagamtide into a Phase 3 development strategy during 2026. Phase 3 matters because it is designed to establish the balance of benefit and risk at scale and create the evidence package needed for potential regulatory submissions.</p><p>Questions Phase 3 needs to answer include optimal dose, oral vs injectable positioning, long-term tolerability, weight-loss plateau, maintenance and performance in people with type 2 diabetes or other obesity-related conditions.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="safety" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-7">Side effects and uncertainty</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Early studies have reported gastrointestinal effects broadly consistent with GLP-1/amylin biology, including nausea and vomiting. But it is too early to write a final “side-effect guide” because there is no UK-approved product label yet.</p><p>The correct position today is: encouraging efficacy signal, incomplete long-term safety picture.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="uk" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-8">When will Amycretin be available in the UK?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>There is no confirmed UK launch date. Phase 3 development has begun, and any eventual UK treatment would still require regulatory authorisation followed by separate commercial and NHS decisions.</p><p>Do not confuse “Phase 3 started” with “available next year”. Drug development timelines can change.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-cagri" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-9">Amycretin vs CagriSema</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="future-table"><tr><th></th><th>Amycretin</th><th>CagriSema</th></tr>
<tr><td>Core biology</td><td>GLP-1 + amylin</td><td>GLP-1 + amylin</td></tr>
<tr><td>Design</td><td>Single unimolecular agonist</td><td>Two-drug combination</td></tr>
<tr><td>Development</td><td>Phase 3 development beginning</td><td>Advanced Phase 3 / regulatory programme</td></tr>
<tr><td>Oral potential</td><td>Yes, studied</td><td>Primarily weekly injectable combination</td></tr></table></div><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-mounjaro" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">10</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-10">Amycretin vs Mounjaro</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Mounjaro is an authorised GIP/GLP-1 treatment with established UK prescribing pathways. Amycretin uses GLP-1 plus amylin and remains investigational. Early efficacy numbers may look competitive, but comparing an approved medicine with an early development candidate using separate trials is not a fair head-to-head.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-reta" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">11</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-11">Amycretin vs Retatrutide</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Retatrutide is a GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist with advanced Phase 3 evidence. Amycretin is a GLP-1/amylin co-agonist at an earlier stage. They represent two different attempts to move beyond GLP-1-only therapy.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="wait" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">12</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-12">Should I wait for Amycretin?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>If you need treatment now, no sensible guide should tell you to delay appropriate care for an investigational medicine. If you're doing well without medication, keep going. If future Amycretin approval eventually offers a material advantage, you can reconsider then.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="questions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">13</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-13">Questions you haven't thought to ask yet</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul class="future-questions"><li>Will oral and injectable Amycretin deliver similar long-term results?</li><li>Will oral dosing have food or water restrictions?</li><li>Will the amylin component change nausea patterns?</li><li>How will it compare directly with CagriSema?</li><li>What maintenance dose will be needed?</li><li>Would the convenience of a pill justify switching from a treatment already working?</li></ul><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="shift" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">14</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-14">Shift Says</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">15</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-15">Our take</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Amycretin is genuinely interesting because it could combine two powerful satiety pathways in one molecule and potentially offer an oral route. But it is still a development programme, not a UK treatment decision today.</p><p>Watch the Phase 3 evidence. Don't buy the hype before the evidence arrives.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="print" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">16</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-16">Printable summary</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><div class="future-print"><h3>Amycretin checklist</h3><ul><li>Investigational, not routine UK treatment.</li><li>Single GLP-1 + amylin co-agonist.</li><li>Oral and injectable forms are being developed.</li><li>Phase 3 is now the important next evidence step.</li><li>Do not delay appropriate treatment today solely to wait for it.</li></ul><button class="btn btn-primary" onclick="window.print()">Print / Save</button></div><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="faq" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">17</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-17">FAQs</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>Is Amycretin available in the UK?</h3><p>No. It remains investigational.</p><h3>Is Amycretin the same as CagriSema?</h3><p>No. Both target GLP-1 and amylin biology, but Amycretin is a single molecule while CagriSema combines semaglutide with cagrilintide.</p><h3>Can Amycretin be taken as a tablet?</h3><p>Oral and injectable formulations have been studied.</p><h3>Has Amycretin reached Phase 3?</h3><p>Novo Nordisk advanced zenagamtide to initiate Phase 3 development in 2026.</p><h3>How much weight did people lose?</h3><p>Early subcutaneous studies reported average losses in the mid-20% range at higher studied doses, but these are not Phase 3 outcomes.</p><h3>Should I wait for Amycretin?</h3><p>Not if you need appropriate treatment now. Revisit it when Phase 3 and regulatory evidence are mature.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="sources" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">18</span><h2 id="rp-guides--amycretin-uk-guide-18">Sources & further reading</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Future-medicine status changes quickly, so we prioritise regulator, manufacturer and official trial sources and date-stamp the page.</p><ul class="future-source"><li><a href="https://annualreport.novonordisk.com/2025/introducing-novo-nordisk/2025-at-a-glance.html" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank">Novo Nordisk 2025 Annual Report – pipeline progress</a></li><li><a href="https://sciencehub.novonordisk.com/congresses/ada2026/mora.html" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank">Novo Nordisk Science Hub – zenagamtide / amycretin 2026</a></li><li><a href="https://www.novonordisk.com/science-and-technology/r-d-pipeline.html" rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank">Novo Nordisk R&D pipeline</a></li></ul><h3>Put it head-to-head</h3><p>Want to see how this option stacks up against another future medicine — or against <a href="/mounjaro" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Mounjaro</a> or <a href="/wegovy" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Wegovy</a>?</p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/future-medicines-comparison">Open comparison checker</a><aside class="editorial-note-v2222">

answer"><h2>CagriSema availability: what does the latest checked announcement say?</h2><p>Novo Nordisk still described CagriSema as an investigational product in its 21 September 2026 announcement. That announcement reports new trial results; it does not establish UK authorisation, an NHS rollout date or a UK treatment price. This is a guide to the research, and SHIFT is not supplying CagriSema.</p><p><a href="https://www.novonordisk.com/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=916774">Novo Nordisk announcement, 21 September 2026</a></p></aside></div><div class="qr-block"><p class="byline-v12">Written and researched by <a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Matt O’Brien</a>, founder of Shift Some Timber.</p></div><div class="qr-block"><aside aria-label="Medicine trust and review status" class="medicine-trust-panel-v42l"><div><strong>Shift medicine standard</strong><span>Emerging/research topic — check the page for current UK status.</span></div><div><strong>Shift service status</strong><span>Evidence-led medicine information and decision support, researched from UK guidance, regulatory sources and published evidence.</span></div><div><strong>Suitability</strong><span>A qualified clinician must decide whether a medicine is appropriate for an individual.</span></div><div><strong>Price & provider</strong><span>No Shift treatment price or treatment provider applies while Shift is not supplying medication.</span></div><div><strong>Evidence review</strong><span>August 2026. →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#alternatives">What can I choose now? →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#questions">Questions you haven't thought to ask →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#faq">FAQs →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#shift">Shift Says →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#print">Printable summary →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#sources">Sources →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="status" aria-hidden="true"></span></div><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-feature"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-1">CagriSema UK status: where things actually stand</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>CagriSema is not yet a routine UK prescription treatment.</h3><p>The guide’s 8 August 2026 status summary described CagriSema as investigational in Europe and the UK. Novo Nordisk submitted it for obesity approval in the United States in December 2025, with a US regulatory decision expected later in 2026. The company has said the European regulatory pathway is still linked to further data from the REDEFINE 3 cardiovascular-outcomes programme.</p><p>So this is a future-medicine guide, not a buying guide. If somebody is advertising “CagriSema” as a normal UK treatment today, that is not the same as receiving an approved medicine through a standard regulated prescribing pathway.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-2">What is CagriSema?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>CagriSema is a fixed-dose combination being developed by Novo Nordisk. It brings together two medicines in one once-weekly injection:</p><div class="cagri-grid">
<div class="cagri-card"><h3>Semaglutide</h3><p>A long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist — the same active ingredient used in <a href="/wegovy" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Wegovy</a> for weight management.</p></div>
<div class="cagri-card"><h3>Cagrilintide</h3><p>A long-acting amylin analogue designed to work on appetite and satiety through a different hormonal pathway.</p></div>
<div class="cagri-card"><h3>The combination</h3><p>The idea is to combine two complementary appetite-regulation pathways rather than simply pushing one pathway harder.</p></div>
</div><p>The principal Phase 3 obesity dose studied has combined cagrilintide 2.4 mg with semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="amylin" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-3">What is amylin — and why does cagrilintide matter?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Amylin is a hormone normally released alongside insulin after eating. It helps signal fullness and can influence how quickly food leaves the stomach. Cagrilintide is a long-acting amylin analogue designed to reproduce some of those effects in a form suitable for weekly treatment.</p><p>This matters because most modern obesity medicines have focused heavily on GLP-1 and related incretin pathways. CagriSema adds a second, different satiety pathway through amylin.</p><strong>Shift translation:</strong><p>Wegovy says “GLP-1”. <a href="/mounjaro" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Mounjaro</a> says “GIP + GLP-1”. CagriSema says “GLP-1 + amylin”. Same broad objective — reduce appetite and improve metabolic control — but via a different combination of biological signals.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="mechanism" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-4">How does CagriSema work?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Semaglutide can reduce hunger, increase fullness and improve glucose-dependent insulin signalling. Cagrilintide adds amylin-receptor activity, which is also associated with satiety and reduced food intake.</p><p>The appeal is not that one ingredient is “stronger” than the other. The scientific question is whether combining them produces more clinically useful weight loss, glycaemic benefit or tolerability than either component alone.</p><p>That is exactly what the REDEFINE and REIMAGINE programmes are designed to test.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="redefine1" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-5">What did REDEFINE 1 show in obesity?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>REDEFINE 1 was the first pivotal Phase 3 trial of CagriSema in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes. It enrolled 3,417 participants and compared CagriSema with semaglutide 2.4 mg, cagrilintide 2.4 mg and placebo over 68 weeks.</p><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="cagri-table"><thead><tr><th>Treatment</th><th>Mean weight change at 68 weeks</th><th>Context</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg</td><td>22.7% under the efficacy estimand</td><td>Largest average loss in the trial.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Semaglutide 2.4 mg</td><td>Lower than CagriSema</td><td>Established GLP-1 benchmark.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Cagrilintide 2.4 mg</td><td>Lower than CagriSema</td><td>Shows the contribution of the amylin component alone.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Placebo</td><td>2.3%</td><td>Background comparison.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><p>More than 40% of participants receiving CagriSema achieved weight loss of at least 25% in the efficacy analysis.</p><strong>Do not turn trial averages into guarantees.</strong><p>Different estimands, adherence patterns, dose modifications and individual biology all change the result a person might experience in real life.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="diabetes" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-6">What does the diabetes evidence show?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>CagriSema is also being studied in type 2 diabetes through the REIMAGINE programme. In REIMAGINE 2, Novo Nordisk reported that CagriSema 2.4/2.4 mg produced an average 14.2% weight reduction at 68 weeks under the efficacy estimand, compared with 10.2% for semaglutide 2.4 mg, while also producing a larger reduction in HbA1c.</p><p>That is relevant because people with type 2 diabetes often lose less weight on obesity medicines than people without diabetes. It also suggests the combination may have a role that extends beyond body weight alone.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="trials" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-7">The wider CagriSema Phase 3 programme</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="cagri-table"><thead><tr><th>Programme</th><th>What it studies</th><th>Why it matters</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>REDEFINE 1</td><td>Obesity / overweight without diabetes</td><td>Pivotal obesity efficacy and safety.</td></tr>
<tr><td>REDEFINE 2</td><td>Obesity / overweight with type 2 diabetes</td><td>Weight loss in a harder-to-treat population.</td></tr>
<tr><td>REDEFINE 3</td><td>Cardiovascular outcomes</td><td>Tests whether benefits extend to major cardiovascular events and long-term safety.</td></tr>
<tr><td>REDEFINE 4</td><td>CagriSema vs tirzepatide</td><td>Direct head-to-head evidence rather than comparing separate trials.</td></tr>
<tr><td>REDEFINE 9</td><td>Lower maintenance doses</td><td>May clarify whether everybody needs the full dose long term.</td></tr>
<tr><td>REDEFINE 11</td><td>Further weight-loss potential</td><td>Explores longer or different treatment strategies.</td></tr>
<tr><td>High-dose programme</td><td>Higher-dose CagriSema</td><td>Tests whether more effect is achievable while preserving tolerability.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><p>Novo Nordisk's 2026 materials indicate that REDEFINE 3 cardiovascular-outcome data remain important to the European regulatory pathway.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="results" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-8">How much weight could CagriSema eventually help people lose?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The headline Phase 3 obesity number is around 22.7% average weight reduction at 68 weeks in participants who adhered to treatment under the efficacy estimand.</p><p>For context only, somebody starting at 20 stone would mathematically see 22.7% equal to about 4.5 stone. That is <strong>not</strong> a forecast for an individual person.</p><p>The important comparison is not just “is the average number big?” but:</p><ul>
<li>How many people achieve clinically meaningful thresholds?</li>
<li>How many can tolerate treatment?</li>
<li>How does it compare directly with tirzepatide?</li>
<li>What happens after treatment stops?</li>
<li>What is the long-term cardiovascular and safety profile?</li>
<li>What dose is actually needed for maintenance?</li>
</ul><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="safety" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-9">Side effects and tolerability</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Across CagriSema trials, gastrointestinal effects have been the main adverse-event category, consistent with incretin and amylin-based treatment. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are all important practical considerations.</p><p>The flexible-dose design in REDEFINE 1 is worth noting because treatment was not simply “everybody must reach the maximum no matter what”. Dose modification and tolerability are part of how a real obesity medicine needs to work.</p><p>Long-term cardiovascular outcomes, maintenance-dose strategies and higher-dose studies are still adding to the safety and benefit picture.</p><strong>What we know vs what we don't:</strong><p>We have mature Phase 3 weight-loss data. We do not yet have a final UK product label, UK contraindication list, UK titration schedule or UK long-term prescribing guidance because the medicine is not yet authorised here.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="uk" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">10</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-10">When could CagriSema become available in the UK?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>There is no confirmed UK launch date we can responsibly publish today.</p><p>Novo Nordisk filed CagriSema for obesity approval in the United States in December 2025, with a US decision expected in Q4 2026. Company materials in June 2026 said the EU regulatory pathway for obesity and type 2 diabetes is pending REDEFINE 3 cardiovascular-outcomes data.</p><p>That means a UK pathway could differ in timing from the US. Even after regulatory approval, commercial launch timing and NHS availability are separate questions.</p><strong>Shift Says</strong><p>If somebody has turned “promising regulatory progress” into an exact UK launch date, they have probably filled in the blanks themselves.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="nhs" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">11</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-11">Will CagriSema be available on the NHS?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>There is currently no NHS CagriSema pathway because it is not an authorised UK treatment.</p><p>If it is approved in future, NHS use would depend on NICE assessment, cost-effectiveness, commissioning and any prioritisation rules. Mounjaro already demonstrates why regulatory approval and NHS availability are not the same thing.</p><p>So a future NHS decision will need to consider not only how much weight CagriSema can help people lose, but also outcomes, safety, comparative effectiveness, price and how it fits against existing treatments.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="cost" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">12</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-12">What will CagriSema cost privately?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>No legitimate UK private retail price exists yet because there is no authorised UK CagriSema product.</p><p>Future pricing could be influenced by Wegovy, Mounjaro, dose requirements, competition, provider services and whether the combination is positioned as a premium treatment.</p><strong>Do not treat online “CagriSema” prices as an indication of the future licensed price.</strong><p>An unapproved online product is not the same thing as a regulated future medicine supplied through a qualified prescriber and registered pharmacy.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-wegovy" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">13</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-13">CagriSema vs Wegovy</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="cagri-table"><thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>CagriSema</th><th>Wegovy</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Active pathways</td><td>Amylin + GLP-1</td><td>GLP-1</td></tr>
<tr><td>Components</td><td>Cagrilintide + semaglutide</td><td>Semaglutide</td></tr>
<tr><td>UK status</td><td>Investigational</td><td>Authorised</td></tr>
<tr><td>Obesity Phase 3 headline</td><td>22.7% mean weight loss in REDEFINE 1 efficacy analysis</td><td>Strong established obesity evidence and real-world use</td></tr>
<tr><td>Routine treatment today</td><td>No</td><td>Yes, if clinically appropriate</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><p>CagriSema is essentially asking whether adding long-acting amylin activity to semaglutide can produce a meaningfully better clinical outcome than semaglutide alone. REDEFINE 1 suggests stronger weight loss, but availability, cost, long-term outcomes and tolerability still matter.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-mounjaro" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">14</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-14">CagriSema vs Mounjaro</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>This is likely to become one of the most commercially and clinically important obesity-treatment comparisons.</p><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="cagri-table"><thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>CagriSema</th><th>Mounjaro</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Mechanism</td><td>Amylin + GLP-1</td><td>GIP + GLP-1</td></tr>
<tr><td>Company</td><td>Novo Nordisk</td><td>Eli Lilly</td></tr>
<tr><td>UK today</td><td>Not yet authorised</td><td>Authorised</td></tr>
<tr><td>Direct head-to-head</td><td colspan="2">REDEFINE 4 directly compared CagriSema with tirzepatide. Novo Nordisk announced results on 23 February 2026.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><p>In the 809-participant, open-label REDEFINE 4 trial, Novo reported 23.0% mean weight loss with CagriSema versus 25.5% with tirzepatide at 84 weeks under the efficacy estimand; the treatment-regimen figures were 20.2% and 23.6%. CagriSema did not meet the primary non-inferiority endpoint. These manufacturer-reported results concern the studied doses and population, not every individual treatment decision. <a href="https://www.novonordisk.com/content/nncorp/global/en/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=916501">Read the REDEFINE 4 announcement</a>. Comparison evidence checked 3 October 2026.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-reta" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">15</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-15">CagriSema vs Retatrutide</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>These two future medicines take very different routes.</p><ul>
<li><strong>CagriSema:</strong> combines amylin with GLP-1.</li>
<li><strong>Retatrutide:</strong> combines GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptor activity.</li>
</ul><p>Retatrutide has produced larger headline Phase 3 weight-loss percentages in some studies, while CagriSema builds on the very mature semaglutide platform and introduces amylin as a complementary pathway.</p><p>Neither is currently a routine UK prescribing option, and each still has important evidence and regulatory questions outstanding.</p><p><a href="/guides/retatrutide-uk-guide"><strong>Read the Retatrutide guide →</strong></a></p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="wait" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">16</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-16">Should I wait for CagriSema?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><div class="cagri-grid">
<div class="cagri-card"><h3>If you need treatment now</h3><p>Do not delay appropriate care solely to wait for a future medicine. Mounjaro, Wegovy, Orlistat, lifestyle support, NHS services and surgery already exist.</p></div>
<div class="cagri-card"><h3>If you're doing well now</h3><p>There is no prize for switching simply because something newer arrives. Reassess only if the new option solves a real problem for you.</p></div>
<div class="cagri-card"><h3>If current treatment isn't enough</h3><p>Speak to a clinician about current alternatives rather than self-sourcing an investigational product.</p></div>
</div><p>The sensible question is not “is CagriSema coming?” It is “would waiting materially improve my health decision compared with the options I can safely use now?”</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="alternatives" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">17</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-17">What can I choose today instead?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="cagri-table"><thead><tr><th>Option</th><th>Available now?</th><th>Why consider it?</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>Mounjaro</td><td>Yes</td><td>Strong current obesity evidence; dual GIP/GLP-1 pathway.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Wegovy</td><td>Yes</td><td>Semaglutide-based GLP-1 treatment with mature obesity evidence.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Orlistat</td><td>Yes</td><td>Non-incretin oral option.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Lifestyle-first</td><td>Yes</td><td>Free or low-cost, builds foundations needed with or without medication.</td></tr>
<tr><td>NHS specialist support</td><td>Yes for eligible people</td><td>Multidisciplinary route that may include medication or surgery.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Bariatric surgery</td><td>Yes for suitable people</td><td>Established, powerful intervention for severe obesity.</td></tr>
<tr><td>CagriSema</td><td><strong>No routine UK treatment</strong></td><td>Future option subject to regulatory approval.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><p><a href="/compare-weight-loss-treatments"><strong>Compare current medicines →</strong></a></p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="questions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">18</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-18">Questions you haven't thought to ask yet</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul class="cagri-questions">
<li>Will I need the full 2.4/2.4 mg dose long term?</li>
<li>Could lower maintenance doses reduce cost or side effects?</li>
<li>How will it compare directly with tirzepatide?</li>
<li>Will cardiovascular-outcomes data change who should use it?</li>
<li>Will the UK licence be narrower than expected?</li>
<li>Will the NHS prioritise it differently from Mounjaro?</li>
<li>Will I be able to switch from Wegovy without restarting titration?</li>
<li>What happens if I tolerate semaglutide but not cagrilintide?</li>
<li>Would a standalone amylin medicine suit some people better?</li>
<li>How will long-term weight regain compare after stopping?</li>
<li>Will amylin-related effects create different appetite or nausea patterns?</li>
<li>Would the extra weight loss justify a higher private price?</li>
</ul><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="faq" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">19</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-19">CagriSema FAQs</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>Is CagriSema available in the UK?</h3><p>No. As of 8 August 2026 it is not a routine authorised UK prescription treatment.</p><h3>What is in CagriSema?</h3><p>It combines cagrilintide, a long-acting amylin analogue, with semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist.</p><h3>Is CagriSema just stronger Wegovy?</h3><p>No. It contains semaglutide but adds a second active medicine, cagrilintide, acting through the amylin pathway.</p><h3>How often is CagriSema injected?</h3><p>The Phase 3 programme uses once-weekly subcutaneous injections.</p><h3>How much weight was lost in REDEFINE 1?</h3><p>Novo Nordisk reported 22.7% mean weight reduction at 68 weeks under the efficacy estimand.</p><h3>Is CagriSema better than Mounjaro?</h3><p>REDEFINE 4 did not demonstrate non-inferiority to tirzepatide for weight loss. See the dated results and limitations in the comparison section.</p><h3>Is it better than Wegovy?</h3><p>REDEFINE 1 showed greater average weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg, but overall suitability also depends on safety, tolerability, approval and long-term outcomes.</p><h3>Will CagriSema be on the NHS?</h3><p>There is no current NHS pathway. Any future NHS use would depend on regulatory approval and NICE/commissioning decisions.</p><h3>How much will it cost?</h3><p>There is no approved UK retail price yet.</p><h3>When will it launch in the UK?</h3><p>There is no confirmed UK launch date.</p><h3>Has CagriSema been filed anywhere?</h3><p>Novo Nordisk filed for obesity approval in the US in December 2025.</p><h3>What are the main side effects?</h3><p>Gastrointestinal effects have been the main adverse-event category in trials.</p><h3>Should I wait for CagriSema?</h3><p>Not automatically. If your health requires treatment now, discuss currently authorised options with a clinician.</p><h3>Can I buy CagriSema online now?</h3><p>An online product is not equivalent to a future authorised CagriSema medicine. Do not assume authenticity, quality or medical supervision.</p><h3>What is cagrilintide?</h3><p>It is a long-acting amylin analogue being developed to enhance satiety and support weight management.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="shift" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">20</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-20">Shift Says</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">21</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-21">If you were our brother...</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>We'd absolutely keep CagriSema on the radar. The Phase 3 evidence is strong enough that this is clearly more than a speculative research project.</p><p>But we would not delay sensible treatment now just because the next medicine might be better. And we certainly would not buy something labelled “CagriSema” from an unregulated website before there is an approved UK product.</p><p>When it eventually becomes a genuine option, the questions will be simple: <strong>does it work better for you, can you tolerate it, is the extra benefit worth the cost, and what is the long-term plan?</strong></p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="print" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">22</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-22">Printable decision summary</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><div class="cagri-print">
<h3>Before I make any decision around CagriSema...</h3>
<ul>
<li>I understand it is not yet a routine UK treatment.</li>
<li>I understand CagriSema combines semaglutide with cagrilintide.</li>
<li>I know the headline 22.7% weight-loss figure is a trial average, not a promise.</li>
<li>I know direct comparison with tirzepatide is more important than social-media scorecards.</li>
<li>I understand European/UK regulatory timing is not the same as US filing.</li>
<li>I have considered treatment options available today.</li>
<li>I will not buy an unapproved online product simply because it uses the CagriSema name.</li>
</ul>

</div><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="sources" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">23</span><h2 id="rp-guides--cagrisema-uk-guide-23">Sources & further reading</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Because CagriSema is still developing, we prioritise primary trial registries, Novo Nordisk's formal clinical/investor disclosures and regulator materials.
