→</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#wait">Should I wait? →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#questions">Questions you haven't thought to ask →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#shift">Shift Says →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#print">Printable summary →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#faq">FAQs →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><a href="#sources">Sources →</a></div><div class="qr-block"><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="status" aria-hidden="true"></span></div><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-feature"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-1">MariTide: where it stands now</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>MariTide remains investigational and is now in Phase 3.</h3><p>Amgen's maridebart cafraglutide — MariTide — is being evaluated in the <strong>MARITIME Phase 3 programme</strong> for obesity and obesity-related conditions. It is not a routine UK prescription treatment today.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-2">What is MariTide?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>MariTide is short for <strong>maridebart cafraglutide</strong>. It is an antibody-peptide conjugate rather than a conventional weekly GLP-1 injection.</p><p>Its design links a GLP-1 receptor agonist component with an antibody directed at the GIP receptor, producing a biological strategy that is almost the mirror image of tirzepatide's GIP agonism.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="mechanism" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-3">How does MariTide work?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><div class="future-grid"><div class="future-card"><h3>GLP-1 receptor agonism</h3><p>Supports appetite reduction and satiety.</p></div>
<div class="future-card"><h3>GIP receptor antagonism</h3><p>Blocks rather than activates the GIP receptor — a distinctive approach informed partly by human genetics.</p></div>
<div class="future-card"><h3>Antibody-peptide design</h3><p>Creates a long-acting medicine that Amgen is studying for monthly or potentially less frequent dosing.</p></div></div><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="monthly" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-4">Why could monthly dosing matter?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Most current injectable obesity medicines are taken weekly. MariTide is being developed around <strong>monthly or less frequent</strong> administration.</p><p>That could reduce treatment burden substantially. Twelve injections a year feels very different from fifty-two. The trade-off is that a very long-acting medicine also needs a carefully understood safety and tolerability profile because you cannot simply “undo” a dose once given.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="phase2" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-5">What did Phase 2 show?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Amgen's Phase 2 study reported up to approximately <strong>20% average weight loss at 52 weeks</strong> in people with obesity or overweight without type 2 diabetes, under the efficacy estimand, without an observed weight-loss plateau at that time point. Participants with type 2 diabetes lost up to around 17% on average and also showed substantial HbA1c improvement.</p><p>Those results were strong enough for Amgen to move into a broad Phase 3 programme.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="phase3" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-6">What is the MARITIME Phase 3 programme?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>MARITIME is the umbrella programme studying MariTide across obesity and obesity-related disease. Amgen describes it as evaluating the medicine in obesity/overweight and conditions including type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular-related risk.</p><p>Phase 3 is particularly important for MariTide because it needs to confirm whether less-frequent dosing remains effective and acceptable across larger populations and longer follow-up.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="safety" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-7">Side effects and safety</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Gastrointestinal adverse effects such as nausea and vomiting have been important during clinical development, and Amgen has explored dose-escalation approaches designed to improve tolerability.</p><p>Because MariTide is long-acting, practical questions around initiation, dose spacing, side-effect duration and discontinuation will matter heavily if it reaches approval.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="uk" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-8">When might MariTide reach the UK?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>There is no confirmed UK launch date. Phase 3 development is ongoing, so any routine UK use remains dependent on completed trials, regulatory submission, MHRA authorisation and subsequent launch decisions.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-mounjaro" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-9">MariTide vs Mounjaro</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table class="future-table"><tr><th></th><th>MariTide</th><th>Mounjaro</th></tr>
<tr><td>GLP-1</td><td>Agonist</td><td>Agonist</td></tr>
<tr><td>GIP pathway</td><td>Receptor antagonist</td><td>Receptor agonist</td></tr>
<tr><td>Dosing ambition</td><td>Monthly or less frequent</td><td>Weekly</td></tr>
<tr><td>UK status</td><td>Investigational</td><td>Authorised</td></tr></table></div><p>This is a fascinating scientific contrast: both target GLP-1 and the GIP axis, but they manipulate GIP in opposite directions.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="vs-reta" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">10</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-10">MariTide vs Retatrutide</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Retatrutide is a weekly triple agonist acting on GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon. MariTide combines GLP-1 agonism with GIP receptor antagonism and aims for much less frequent dosing.</p><p>Retatrutide currently has the more dramatic Phase 3 headline weight-loss figures; MariTide's potential differentiator is dosing convenience plus a unique mechanism.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="who" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">11</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-11">Who might eventually prefer MariTide?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li>People who want fewer injections.</li><li>People who struggle to maintain a weekly treatment routine.</li><li>People for whom a long-acting medicine proves more convenient and equally tolerable.</li><li>Potentially people who respond differently to GIP antagonism than to GIP agonism — if future evidence supports that distinction.</li></ul><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="wait" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">12</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-12">Should I wait for MariTide?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>No one should delay needed treatment simply because monthly dosing sounds appealing. Current options already have extensive evidence and real UK prescribing pathways. MariTide becomes a real decision only when Phase 3 evidence and regulation make it one.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="questions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">13</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-13">Questions you haven't thought to ask yet</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul class="future-questions"><li>If I feel unwell after a monthly dose, how long could effects last?</li><li>Will titration require shorter intervals before monthly maintenance?</li><li>Will monthly dosing actually improve adherence?</li><li>How will it compare with weekly drugs in a true head-to-head trial?</li><li>Could less frequent dosing reduce pharmacy and delivery costs?</li><li>What happens when stopping such a long-acting medicine?</li></ul><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="shift" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">14</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-14">Shift Says</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">15</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-15">Our take</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>MariTide may be the most interesting “convenience” play in the pipeline. If monthly dosing can deliver strong weight loss with acceptable tolerability, it could genuinely change what long-term treatment feels like.</p><p>But convenience is only valuable once safety, efficacy and durability are proven at Phase 3 scale.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="print" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">16</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-16">Printable summary</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><div class="future-print"><h3>MariTide checklist</h3><ul><li>Investigational antibody-peptide conjugate.</li><li>GLP-1 agonism + GIP receptor antagonism.</li><li>Being studied for monthly or less frequent dosing.</li><li>Phase 2 showed up to ~20% average loss at 52 weeks in obesity without diabetes.</li><li>Now in the Phase 3 MARITIME programme.</li></ul><button class="btn btn-primary" onclick="window.print()">Print / Save</button></div><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="faq" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">17</span><h2 id="rp-guides--maritide-uk-guide-17">FAQs</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>Is MariTide available in the UK?</h3><p>No. It remains investigational.</p><h3>What does MariTide stand for?</h3><p>It is the short name for maridebart cafraglutide.</p><h3>How often might MariTide be taken?</h3><p>Amgen is studying monthly or potentially less frequent dosing.</p><h3>How much weight loss was seen in Phase 2?</h3><p>Up to approximately 20% average weight loss at 52 weeks in participants without type 2 diabetes.</p><h3>Is MariTide a GLP-1?</h3><p>It includes GLP-1 receptor agonism but also blocks the GIP receptor.</p><h3>Has MariTide reached Phase 3?</h3><p>Yes. <section class="rr-section" id="mechanism"><span id="what"></span><p class="rr-eyebrow">A mechanism is the starting point</p><div class="rr-two"><div><h2>What does “triple agonist” mean?</h2><p class="rr-intro">Retatrutide is one investigational molecule that activates GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors. “Triple” identifies its targets; it does not mean three times the benefit. “GLP-3” is an inaccurate nickname. <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-lilly-faq" aria-label="See source: lilly-faq">Source</a></p></div><div class="rr-note" style="margin-top:0"><p><strong>A receptor diagram cannot prove a health outcome.</strong><br>Claims about weight, heart health, liver health or energy expenditure need evidence for that specific outcome. We keep the mechanism separate from what trials have actually measured.</p></div></div></section>

<section class="rr-section" id="uk-pathway"><p class="rr-eyebrow">Evidence, approval and access are separate</p><h2>What would have to happen in the UK?</h2><p class="rr-intro">A positive study is one piece of the picture. These stages should never be collapsed into an invented release date.</p><div class="rr-pathway"><div class="rr-path-step rr-active"><span class="rr-number">01 · EVIDENCE</span><h3>Study results are assessed</h3><p>Published trials and sponsor announcements contribute different types of evidence.</p><span class="rr-state">RESULTS AVAILABLE</span></div><div class="rr-path-step"><span class="rr-number">02 · REGULATION</span><h3>UK authorisation is a separate decision</h3><p>The checked MHRA source says retatrutide is not authorised. <section class="rr-section rr-faq" id="questions"><span id="faq"></span><p class="rr-eyebrow">Short answers. Sources close by.</p><h2>The questions people are asking.</h2><details><summary>Is “Reta” the same as retatrutide?</summary><p>It is an informal abbreviation used online. The name on a vial or a seller’s page does not establish that the contents match the investigational medicine used in an authorised trial. <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-mhra" aria-label="See source: mhra">Source</a> <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-lilly-faq" aria-label="See source: lilly-faq">Source</a></p></details><details><summary>Is retatrutide better than Mounjaro or Wegovy?</summary><p>Different trial percentages cannot establish a winner. The populations, time points, analyses and safety findings must match the comparison being made. The latest direct result shown here compares retatrutide with Ozempic 2 mg in type 2 diabetes, not those weight-management products. <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-transcend" aria-label="See source: transcend">Source</a></p></details><details><summary>When will it launch, and what will it cost?</summary><p>This source check did not establish a confirmed UK launch date or UK launch price. Prices advertised by sellers of unauthorised products do not establish either. <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-mhra" aria-label="See source: mhra">Source</a> <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-lilly-faq" aria-label="See source: lilly-faq">Source</a></p></details><details><summary>Can I buy or reserve it through SHIFT?</summary><p>No. This is an evidence guide. SHIFT is not offering retatrutide, accepting reservations or providing a buying route.</p></details><details><summary>Why do the charts show different weight-loss figures?</summary><p>Study populations and analysis methods differ. The chart selector shows two analyses of TRIUMPH-1; the safety section concerns TRIUMPH-2, which included type 2 diabetes. All values remain available in ordinary text and tables. <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-triumph1" aria-label="See source: triumph1">Source</a> <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-triumph1-sponsor" aria-label="See source: triumph1-sponsor">Source</a> <a class="rr-ref" href="#src-triumph2" aria-label="See source: triumph2">Source</a></p></details></section>
</article><div class="rr-retained-context"><section class="rr-reta-section" id="illegal"><h2>What about “Reta peptides”, pens or vials sold online?</h2><p>The MHRA warns against products sold as retatrutide and describes concerns about unregulated medicines’ quality and safety. A label or seller’s certificate does not establish UK authorisation. <a href="#r1">[1]</a></p><p>Research reporting should not become a shopping guide for an unapproved product. This page therefore contains no seller recommendations, affiliate buying links, preparation instructions or reconstitution calculator. Someone concerned about a product they have used should seek professional advice and can consult the MHRA’s reporting information. <a href="#r1">[1]</a></p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="cost"><h2>How much will retatrutide cost in the UK?</h2><p><strong>This review has not verified a UK launch price.</strong> Prices advertised for products sold online do not tell us what an authorised future treatment would cost. A predicted figure is not made more reliable by placing “UK” beside it.</p><p>If a legitimate UK price is announced later, a useful comparison would need the supply duration, formulation, required consultation and any compulsory charges. Until then, there is no defensible price table for this guide to publish.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="nhs"><h2>Will retatrutide be available on the NHS?</h2><p>No routine NHS retatrutide pathway is established by the sources reviewed here. Authorisation and an NHS access decision are separate questions. The NHS explains that weight-management care can involve lifestyle support, selected medicines and, for some people, specialist assessment or surgery. <a href="#r7">[7]</a></p><p>Do not apply another medicine’s eligibility rules to retatrutide or assume a private launch would mean immediate NHS access. A future answer would need a specific, dated decision for the relevant NHS system.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="availability"><h2>Is there a confirmed retatrutide UK release date?</h2><p>Lilly’s July announcement describes a planned <strong>US regulatory submission in the first quarter of 2027</strong>. That is a company plan to apply, not an approval or a UK release date. <a href="#r5">[5]</a></p><p>Our update rule is straightforward: report a dated decision once it exists, identify the country and regulator, and explain exactly what changed. A projected study completion, conference presentation or filing must not be rewritten as “available from” a particular month.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="vs-mounjaro"><h2>Retatrutide versus Mounjaro: what is a fair comparison?</h2><p>Retatrutide and Mounjaro’s active ingredient, tirzepatide, are different molecules. Their receptor profiles differ; that description alone cannot establish which produces a better overall outcome for an individual. <a href="#r6">[6]</a></p><p>A useful comparison should put the population, treatment duration, comparator, analysis method and adverse effects side by side. To make a claim about superiority, look for directly relevant comparative evidence rather than choosing the largest percentages from separate studies. This guide makes no head-to-head superiority claim and is not a recommendation to switch treatment.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="vs-wegovy"><h2>Retatrutide versus Wegovy: avoid the percentage contest</h2><p>Wegovy’s active ingredient, semaglutide, acts through GLP-1; retatrutide is being studied as a triple receptor agonist. <a href="#r6">[6]</a> The same comparison questions apply: Who was studied, against what, for how long, and with what harms or discontinuations?</p><p>“More receptors” and “a larger result in another trial” are not substitutes for an individual assessment. A research-stage medicine should not be presented as an available replacement for someone’s current care.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="surgery"><h2>Can a medicine trial be compared with weight-loss surgery?</h2><p>A superficially similar weight percentage does not make two interventions equivalent. Any fair assessment would also need the populations, follow-up, complications, subsequent care and outcomes beyond weight. The NHS describes surgery as a treatment requiring specialist consideration, not simply a percentage target. <a href="#r7">[7]</a></p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="wait"><h2>Should I wait for a future medicine?</h2><p>This guide cannot decide what care you need now. Discuss your current concerns with an appropriately qualified health professional rather than treating an uncertain future launch as a personal treatment plan. A useful question is: “What are my appropriate options now, and what would genuinely change that decision later?”</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="alternatives"><h2>Where can I find information about current care?</h2><p>The <a href="https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/overweight-and-obesity/" rel="noopener noreferrer">NHS overview of overweight and obesity</a> explains current approaches and how to seek help. For background reading on hormone pathways, use our <a href="/glp1-knowledge-centre">GLP-1 Knowledge Centre</a>. These are reading routes, not an offer of retatrutide.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="natural"><h2>What about support without medication?</h2><p>The NHS includes eating, activity and behavioural support within weight-management care. <a href="#r7">[7]</a> Discuss what is appropriate and sustainable for your circumstances. “Medication-free” does not need to mean doing everything alone, and reading research does not commit you to taking a medicine.</p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="prescriber-questions"><h2>Questions worth asking before believing a headline</h2><ul><li>Does the source refer to retatrutide itself, or a different medicine or combination?</li><li>Is this a regulator’s decision, an original paper, a sponsor announcement or someone else’s interpretation?</li><li>Are benefits and adverse effects reported for the same population and follow-up?</li><li>Are trial completers being presented as though they represent everyone who started?</li><li>Does a claim about men have relevant sex-specific evidence? Inclusion of men in a trial is not proof of a benefit unique to men.</li><li>Is an article explaining research, or quietly directing me towards a seller?</li></ul><p>For context, 51.8% of participants in the published Phase 2 obesity trial were men. That does not make it a men-only trial or establish a male-specific treatment recommendation. <a href="#r2">[2]</a></p></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="shift"><h2>The SHIFT take</h2><div class="rr-reta-status"><p><strong>Our interpretation:</strong> the useful story is not just the largest weight-loss percentage. It is whether the evidence becomes strong enough to answer questions about benefit, tolerability, day-to-day function and appropriate access.</p><p>For our readers, we would keep asking what a finding changes in real life—and what it does not. Good information should leave you better equipped to question a claim, not more pressured to buy something. We will distinguish what a source reports from what we infer, and leave an unanswered question unanswered rather than invent certainty.</p></div></section><section class="rr-reta-section" id="print"><h2>A short checklist to keep</h2><ul><li>Check UK status at the regulator source.</li><li>Read trial benefits and adverse effects together.</li><li>Identify the population, duration and analysis.</li><li>Do not confuse a submission plan with a launch.</li><li>Take individual treatment questions to a qualified professional.</li></ul><button class="rr-btn" type="button" onclick="window.print()">Print or save this guide</button></section></div><section class="rr-section" id="sources"><p class="rr-eyebrow">Evidence register</p><h2>Sources stay close.</h2><p class="rr-intro">Selected primary sources checked on 2 November 2026.</p><ol class="rr-source-list"><li id="src-uk-access"><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/get-medicines-to-nhs-patients-earlier-via-the-mhra-nice-aligned-pathway/get-medicines-to-nhs-patients-earlier-via-the-mhra-nice-aligned-pathway" target="_blank" rel="noopener">MHRA / NICE · distinct decisions, aligned assessment</a><span class="rr-source-date">Updated 9 April 2026</span><p>Primary process guidance. Clear caveats where direct evidence does not exist.</p></div></div><div class="qr-graphic qr-graphic-evidence" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true"><p class="qr-micro">The evidence, in context.</p><div class="qr-evidence-stack"><div><span>01</span><strong>Licensed formulation</strong></div><div><span>02</span><strong>Trial evidence</strong></div><div><span>03</span><strong>Access & cost</strong></div></div><p class="qr-graphic-foot">No automatic winner.</p></div></section><div class="qr-body sg-copy"><details class="qr-index" data-qr-decoration><summary>On this page <span aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><nav aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#ut-medication-1">We compare licensed formulations, not just molecules</a><a href="#ut-medication-2">Trial averages are anchors, not forecasts</a><a href="#ut-medication-3">2026 Wegovy caveat</a><a href="#ut-medication-4">Oral Wegovy</a><a href="#ut-medication-5">Ratings</a><a href="#ut-medication-6">NHS accessibility</a><a href="#ut-medication-7">Prices</a><a href="#ut-medication-8">Core evidence anchors</a><a href="#ut-medication-9">No automatic winner.</a><a href="#ut-medication-10">Sources & evidence</a></nav></details><div class="qr-sections"><section class="qr-section qr-feature"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="ut-medication-1" data-section="01">We compare licensed formulations, not just molecules</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Semaglutide now exists in multiple UK products and formulations. Injectable Wegovy, oral Wegovy and Ozempic should not be collapsed into one row because indication, dose, evidence and access differ.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="ut-medication-2" data-section="02">Trial averages are anchors, not forecasts</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>We use pivotal or head-to-head trial results to anchor relative efficacy. Individual results vary, trials have different populations and durations, and cross-trial comparisons are inherently weaker than head-to-head randomised evidence.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="ut-medication-3" data-section="03">2026 Wegovy caveat</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The classic STEP evidence is built around injectable semaglutide 2.4 mg. UK product information now permits 7.2 mg weekly for weight management in adults with obesity if needed after at least four weeks at 2.4 mg. A historical Mounjaro-vs-Wegovy head-to-head using 1.7/2.4 mg semaglutide should therefore not be presented as direct evidence against 7.2 mg.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="ut-medication-4" data-section="04">Oral Wegovy</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Oral Wegovy 25 mg has its own OASIS 4 phase 3b evidence. We do not infer that daily 25 mg oral semaglutide is equivalent to 2.4 mg or 7.2 mg injected semaglutide milligram-for-milligram.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="ut-medication-5" data-section="05">Ratings</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>We present study findings and practical differences without numerical treatment ratings. Separate trials are not a head-to-head ranking, and a study average is not a personal forecast.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="ut-medication-6" data-section="06">NHS accessibility</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>This is deliberately conservative. NICE recommendation, NHS commissioning, phased rollout, specialist-service restrictions and local availability can differ.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="ut-medication-7" data-section="07">Prices</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>We do not freeze a “typical private price” into the core comparison because UK private prices change frequently by provider, dose and supply. Future commercial pages should fetch or regularly review price data rather than fossilising it in a medical guide.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-qr-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="ut-medication-8" data-section="08">Core evidence anchors</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul>
<li>Mounjaro SmPC / SURMOUNT programme</li><li>Wegovy injectable SmPC / STEP programme</li><li>Wegovy 25 mg tablet SmPC / OASIS 4</li><li>Saxenda SmPC / SCALE programme</li><li>NICE technology appraisals and NHS medicine guidance</li>
</ul><div class="med2-banner"><h2 id="ut-medication-9">No automatic winner.</h2><p>A medicine can have stronger average weight-loss evidence and still be the wrong choice for an individual because of contraindications, tolerability, preference, access or maintenance.</p></div><p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="/compare-weight-loss-treatments">Return to Medication Comparison Centre</a></p><aside class="editorial-note-v2222"><h3>Health information</h3><p>General information, not individual medical advice. Lower-dose orlistat 60 mg is a separate pharmacy medicine, with its own eligibility checks and instructions. Do not swap doses or assume that all orlistat is prescription-only.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-orlistat-definitive-uk-guide-2">Who can be considered?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The Xenical 120 mg licence covers BMI of at least 30, or at least 28 with associated risk factors, alongside a reduced-calorie diet. Meeting a BMI threshold does not establish individual suitability. A prescriber or pharmacist needs your medical history and current medicines.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-orlistat-definitive-uk-guide-3">What does taking it involve?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The product information links doses to main meals containing fat. A missed meal or a meal without fat means omitting that dose. Use the instructions supplied with your own prescription. More capsules are not a way to cancel out a large meal.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-orlistat-definitive-uk-guide-4">Side effects and other medicines</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Oily stools, wind with discharge and urgent bowel movements can occur, particularly with higher-fat meals. Tell the clinician about bowel, liver or kidney conditions and all medicines, including warfarin, ciclosporin, thyroid or epilepsy treatment. Ask whether vitamin supplementation or additional monitoring is needed. Persistent or severe symptoms need medical advice.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-orlistat-definitive-uk-guide-5">How will you know whether it is worth continuing?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The 120 mg product information sets a review point: stop treatment if at least 5% of starting body weight has not been lost after 12 weeks. Sources checked 3 October 2026; this is not independent clinical review.</p><p class="standfirst">Ozempic is a diabetes medicine. Weight loss can occur during treatment, but Ozempic does not have a UK weight-management indication.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-ozempic-definitive-uk-guide-2">Is it the same as Wegovy?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The brands share semaglutide as an active ingredient, but have different licensed uses and product instructions. Wegovy is a weight-management brand. Sharing an ingredient does not make pens, doses or prescribing plans interchangeable.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-ozempic-definitive-uk-guide-3">Can my GP prescribe it?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>A clinician can assess diabetes treatment and decide what is appropriate. Asking for Ozempic for weight loss alone is a different question from treating type 2 diabetes. NHS access also depends on the relevant pathway. This page cannot confirm an individual entitlement or prescription.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-ozempic-definitive-uk-guide-4">What should I know about side effects?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Digestive effects such as nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea can occur. Persistent severe abdominal pain needs urgent medical assessment; sudden loss of vision or rapidly worsening eyesight also needs urgent help. Discuss other medicines and any planned anaesthetic with your clinical team. Do not stop or adjust diabetes treatment because of a comparison page.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-ozempic-definitive-uk-guide-5">What if I already take it?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Keep following your own prescription. Sources checked 3 October 2026; this is not independent clinical review.</p><p class="standfirst">Saxenda is a daily prescription injection for weight management. Understanding the daily routine, side effects and review point matters more than treating it as an older version of a weekly jab.</p></div><div class="qr-graphic rest-art" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true"><p class="qr-micro">A clearer next step.</p><div class="rest-rows"><div><span>01</span><strong>What is Saxenda?</strong></div><div><span>02</span><strong>Who can be considered?</strong></div><div><span>03</span><strong>Starting and reviewing treatment</strong></div></div><p>Read the detail. Keep the context.</p></div></section><div class="qr-body sg-copy"><details class="qr-index" data-rp-decoration><summary>On this page <span aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><nav aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-1">What is Saxenda?</a><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-2">Who can be considered?</a><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-3">Starting and reviewing treatment</a><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-4">Side effects need a plan</a><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-5">Questions that make a comparison useful</a><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-6">Do not improvise a switch</a><a href="#rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-7">Keep support after the prescription</a></nav></details><div class="qr-sections"><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-feature"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-1">What is Saxenda?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Saxenda contains liraglutide, a <a href="/glp1-knowledge-centre" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">GLP-1</a> receptor agonist. It is used with reduced-calorie eating and increased physical activity. It is injected daily, unlike weekly products. This page covers adults; it does not assess suitability for a child or teenager.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-2">Who can be considered?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The adult licence covers BMI of at least 30, or BMI from 27 to below 30 with a weight-related condition. The prescriber must assess the whole medical picture. A licence threshold does not guarantee NHS access, private acceptance or available stock.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-3">Starting and reviewing treatment</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The dose is increased gradually under the prescribed schedule. The adult continuation rule is measured after 12 weeks at 3 mg daily: treatment should stop if less than 5% of initial body weight has been lost. That is not simply 12 weeks from the first injection. Agree the review date with your prescriber.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-4">Side effects need a plan</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation can occur. Persistent severe abdominal pain needs urgent medical assessment because pancreatitis is a recognised risk. Seek advice if vomiting prevents adequate drinking. Tell the prescriber about other medicines, especially diabetes treatment; do not change insulin yourself. Read the leaflet for the full warnings.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-5">Questions that make a comparison useful</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li>Can I manage a daily injection and the storage instructions around work or travel?</li><li>Who will advise me if a dose increase is difficult?</li><li>What do I do if supply is interrupted or I miss several days?</li><li>What is the cost at my prescribed maintenance dose, including reviews and supplies?</li><li>If this does not help enough, who reviews the alternatives?</li></ul></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-6">Do not improvise a switch</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Ask the prescriber for written instructions if changing medicine or restarting after a gap. Products are not interchangeable simply because they belong to the same family. Do not combine treatments or copy another person's schedule.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-saxenda-definitive-uk-guide-7">Keep support after the prescription</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Before starting, decide where practical food and movement help will come from and who answers treatment questions. This hub brings the evidence, practical realities and men-specific questions into one place.</p><p class="authority-byline">Written and researched by <a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Matt O’Brien</a>, founder of Shift Some Timber. Evidence reviewed 2026-08-26.</p></div><div class="qr-graphic rest-art" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true"><p class="qr-micro">A clearer next step.</p><div class="rest-rows"><div><span>01</span><strong>Not losing weight on Mounjaro: what should I check?</strong></div><div><span>02</span><strong>What Mounjaro is</strong></div><div><span>03</span><strong>Doses and the usual escalation route</strong></div></div><p>Read the detail. Keep the context.</p></div></section><div class="qr-body sg-copy"><details class="qr-index" data-rp-decoration><summary>On this page <span aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><nav aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#rp-mounjaro-1">Not losing weight on Mounjaro: what should I check?</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-2">What Mounjaro is</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-3">Doses and the usual escalation route</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-4">What trial results can and cannot tell you</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-5">Side effects and safety</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-6">Questions men often miss</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-7">What should I ask before starting with a Mounjaro service?</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-8">NHS and private access</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-9">Frequently asked questions</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-10">Sources you can inspect</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-11">Who wrote this?</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-12">Mounjaro questions: costs, everyday support and treatment changes</a><a href="#rp-mounjaro-13">Support does not have to come from the same place as the prescription</a></nav></details><div class="qr-sections"><div class="qr-block"><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="not-losing-weight-on-mounjaro" aria-hidden="true"></span></div><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-1">Not losing weight on Mounjaro: what should I check?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><strong>One unchanged reading cannot tell you whether Mounjaro is working.</strong> Response varies. Review the pattern, treatment history and side effects with your prescribing service. Do not change your dose, take an extra injection or severely restrict food to force the scale to move.</p><h3>Deal with warning signs before the progress checklist</h3><p><strong>Severe, persistent abdominal pain, with or without nausea or vomiting:</strong> stop using Mounjaro and seek urgent medical help, as the <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15481/pil">UK patient leaflet</a> instructs. Pain may spread to the back. Do not wait for a routine review or a reply from SHIFT.</p><p><strong>Repeated vomiting or difficulty keeping fluids down:</strong> seek urgent advice. If there is trouble breathing, sudden swelling of the mouth or throat, or collapse, call 999. A checklist about weight should never delay care.</p><h3>A useful review checklist</h3><ol><li><strong>Compare comparable readings.</strong> Follow <a href="https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/how-to-record-your-weight/">NHS England’s weighing guidance</a>: use the same scales, a firm level floor and a similar time and clothing. Note dates rather than comparing today's reading with a vague memory. Record constipation and other symptoms too, so the prescribing service has context.</li>
<li><strong>Write down the treatment history.</strong> Record when you started, your prescribed dose, dates of changes and any missed injections. Starting or increasing treatment is not a promise of a particular weekly loss.</li>
<li><strong>Check practical use with the pharmacist or prescriber.</strong> Ask about your pen technique and storage if unsure. Follow the leaflet for your exact product. Do not extract leftover medicine, double a dose or devise your own schedule.</li>
<li><strong>Look at an ordinary working day.</strong> Record meals, snacks, drinks, hunger, movement and sleep without blame. Consider whether long gaps lead to a difficult evening, or whether low appetite is preventing adequate eating. A food record is information for a conversation, not an instruction to eat less and less.</li>
<li><strong>Record tolerability and function.</strong> Tell the service about nausea, vomiting, constipation, poor intake, weakness or difficulty with ordinary activities. Waist, appetite and health measures can provide context; they do not prove the medicine is effective or make warning signs safe to ignore.</li>
<li><strong>Arrange the treatment review.</strong> Ask what progress they expect for your circumstances, when they will review it, and what food or activity support is available. Other conditions and medicines may need consideration. Keep those decisions with an appropriate clinician.</li></ol><h3>When does NICE recommend reviewing a poor response?</h3><p><a href="https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246/resources/a-guide-for-prescribing-medicines-to-manage-overweight-and-obesity-15299628589/chapter/Prescribing-reviewing-and-stopping-tirzepatide">NICE's tirzepatide prescribing guide</a> says that a loss below 5% of starting weight after six months at the highest dose the person can tolerate should lead to a discussion of response and a decision about continued treatment, considering that person's benefits and risks. It also notes that people with type 2 diabetes may lose weight more slowly.</p><p>This is a clinician-led review point, not a rule to stop by yourself after six months from the first injection. Do not wait for that point if you have side effects, difficulty eating or concerns now.</p><h3>A message you can send to your prescribing service</h3><blockquote><p>“I started on [date]. My prescribed dose is [dose], last changed on [date]. My comparable weights are [dates and readings]. My appetite and eating have been [what is true]. I have had [symptoms or none]. Can we review my response, check how I am using the pen and agree the next step?”</p></blockquote><p>Do not delay urgent care to gather those details. My Timber can support ordinary routines; it does not assess treatment response or send this message to a clinician.</p><p>For practical meals, read <a href="/guides/nutrition-protein-calories-meal-planning">food during treatment</a>. For access questions, read <a href="/articles/nhs-weight-loss-drugs">NHS eligibility and routes</a>. This section is information, not a medicine sales offer.</p><p class="shift-practical-note">Practical section added and its linked sources checked 6 October 2026 by the SHIFT editorial team. These are general examples, not a personal diet, exercise or treatment prescription. Independent clinical review is not claimed.</p><div class="authority-facts"><div><strong>Medicine</strong><span>Tirzepatide, supplied in the UK under the Mounjaro brand.</span></div><div><strong>Route</strong><span>A prescription-only injection taken once weekly.</span></div><div><strong>UK position</strong><span>MHRA-authorised for weight management in defined adults.</span></div><div><strong>Strengths</strong><span>2.5mg, 5mg, 7.5mg, 10mg, 12.5mg and 15mg per weekly dose.</span></div></div><nav aria-label="On this page" class="authority-jumps"><strong>On this page</strong><a href="#what-mounjaro-is">What Mounjaro is</a><a href="#doses-and-the-usual-escalation-route">Doses and the usual escalation route</a><a href="#what-trial-results-can-and-cannot-tell-you">What trial results can and cannot tell you</a><a href="#side-effects-and-safety">Side effects and safety</a><a href="#questions-men-often-miss">Questions men often miss</a><a href="#nhs-and-private-access">NHS and private access</a></nav><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what-mounjaro-is" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-2">What Mounjaro is</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Mounjaro contains tirzepatide. It acts through GIP and GLP-1 pathways involved in appetite and metabolic regulation. In the UK it is authorised for weight management in adults with obesity, or adults who are overweight and have at least one qualifying weight-related health problem, alongside diet and physical activity.</p><p>A prescriber must still assess the individual. A licence describes who the medicine may be used for; it does not mean everybody within that broad group should receive it.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="doses-and-the-usual-escalation-route" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-3">Doses and the usual escalation route</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The authorised starting dose is 2.5mg once weekly for four weeks, followed by 5mg once weekly. If clinically appropriate, a prescriber may increase the dose in steps of 2.5mg after at least four weeks at the current dose, up to 15mg once weekly.</p><p>Reaching the maximum dose is not the objective. The appropriate dose is the one a prescriber judges suitable after considering response, side effects, medical history and other medicines. Never copy another person's schedule or accelerate titration yourself.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what-trial-results-can-and-cannot-tell-you" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-4">What trial results can and cannot tell you</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>In the SURMOUNT-1 trial cited by the MHRA, average weight change over 72 weeks was greater with tirzepatide than placebo, with results differing by dose. Those averages came from a controlled study and do not promise an individual result.</p><p>Real-life outcomes are affected by adherence, tolerability, dose, sleep, food, movement, health conditions and whether the surrounding plan is sustainable. Shift reports trial figures with their duration and population rather than turning them into guarantees.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="side-effects-and-safety" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-5">Side effects and safety</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><strong>Get urgent medical help for severe stomach pain that does not go away, especially if it spreads to your back, with or without vomiting.</strong> This can indicate pancreatitis. Do not wait for a routine review or company reply. A clinician must assess it; if pancreatitis is confirmed, the medicine must not be restarted.</p><p>Read the instructions for your exact product and discuss side effects with your prescriber or pharmacist: <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15481/smpc" rel="noopener noreferrer">Mounjaro UK product information</a>. Safety information checked 3 October 2026.</p><p>The most frequently reported effects include nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation. Some symptoms settle as the body adjusts; persistent, severe or worrying symptoms require advice from the treating service or another appropriate healthcare professional.</p><p>Only obtain prescription weight-management medicines through regulated services. Counterfeit and illegally supplied products create a genuine safety risk.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="questions-men-often-miss" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-6">Questions men often miss</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Weight loss can include lean tissue as well as body fat. A sensible plan therefore considers adequate <a href="/articles/protein-for-men-weight-management" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">protein</a>, appropriate strength activity and progressive movement where medically suitable. Men should also discuss relevant medical history, current medicines, blood pressure, <a href="/articles/sleep-apnoea-weight-men" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">sleep apnoea</a> symptoms and any persistent fatigue with the assessing clinician.</p><p>A plateau does not automatically mean the medicine has failed or the dose should change. Weight trends, waist, appetite, side effects, strength, sleep and day-to-day function all help provide context.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="shift-depth-mounjaro-service" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-7">What should I ask before starting with a Mounjaro service?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>A useful comparison covers assessment, supply and care after the first prescription. A headline price cannot tell you whether the service fits your needs. Write the answers down so you can compare the same things.</p><h3>Get these five answers</h3><ol>
<li><strong>Who is responsible?</strong> Ask who assesses and prescribes, which pharmacy dispenses, and how you verify their registration. A brand name alone does not identify every organisation involved.</li>
<li><strong>What information do they need?</strong> Be ready to disclose relevant conditions, other medicines and your treatment history accurately. Ask how the assessment works and what happens if treatment is unsuitable.</li>
<li><strong>What is the whole quote?</strong> Confirm the exact product, supply period, consultation, delivery and any compulsory subscription or follow-up charges. Ask whether the price changes with a later prescribed strength.</li>
<li><strong>How do I get advice?</strong> Find the contact route for side effects, practical pen questions or concerns about response. Ask what to do outside opening hours.</li>
<li><strong>What happens when care changes?</strong> Ask how reviews, pauses, stopping or moving service are handled. Get the relevant cancellation and refund information before agreeing to pay.</li>
</ol><h3>Make an appointment note that answers your question</h3><p>If you are exploring treatment, write down what you want help with, what you have already tried and any health concerns. If you are already taking Mounjaro, use the response checklist above and include your current prescribing service. Do not guess an old dose or leave out another medicine because you think it is unrelated.</p><p>The <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/15481/pil">UK patient leaflet</a> explains why medical history, other medicines and individual instructions matter. Follow your own prescribed instructions; this worksheet does not determine eligibility or a dose.</p><h3>Keep everyday support and prescribing responsibilities clear</h3><p>You can use <a href="/weight-loss-support-for-men">free My Timber support</a> around a prescription supplied elsewhere. It does not transfer responsibility for treatment to SHIFT. Keep the prescribing contact details accessible and take medicine questions directly to that service. Use the <a href="/articles/mounjaro-cost-uk">cost guide</a> for the questions that make two quotes comparable.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="nhs-and-private-access" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="rp-mounjaro-8">NHS and private access</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>MHRA authorisation, NICE recommendations, NHS implementation and a private provider's service criteria are separate questions. Access can vary by nation, local pathway and clinical need. Private treatment should still include proper assessment, prescribing and follow-up.</p><p>Treatment access through SHIFT is subject to clinical assessment and current partner availability. No stock available today.</p><p>Considering the practical side? Any later increase must be directed by the prescriber.</p></details><details><summary>Is Mounjaro automatically available on the NHS?</summary><p>No. MHRA authorisation, NICE recommendations and local NHS implementation are separate. UK adults may encounter a weekly injection, a higher 7.2mg injection route for defined adults with obesity, and a daily tablet with strict administration instructions. This hub keeps those routes separate and understandable.</p><p class="authority-byline">Written and researched by <a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Matt O’Brien</a>, founder of Shift Some Timber. Evidence reviewed 2026-08-26.</p></div><div class="qr-graphic rest-art" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true"><p class="qr-micro">A clearer next step.</p><div class="rest-rows"><div><span>01</span><strong>What Wegovy is</strong></div><div><span>02</span><strong>The weekly injection route</strong></div><div><span>03</span><strong>The daily Wegovy pill</strong></div></div><p>Read the detail. Keep the context.</p></div></section><div class="qr-body sg-copy"><details class="qr-index" data-rp-decoration><summary>On this page <span aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><nav aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#rp-wegovy-1">What Wegovy is</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-2">The weekly injection route</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-3">The daily Wegovy pill</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-4">Results and expectations</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-5">How do I compare Wegovy tablets and injections for my actual week?</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-6">Side effects and muscle retention</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-7">Access and what happens next</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-8">Frequently asked questions</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-9">Sources you can inspect</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-10">Who wrote this?</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-11">Wegovy questions: side effects, costs and everyday support</a><a href="#rp-wegovy-12">Keep practical support around the prescription</a></nav></details><div class="qr-sections"><div class="qr-block"><div class="authority-facts"><div><strong>Medicine</strong><span>Semaglutide under the Wegovy brand.</span></div><div><strong>Routes</strong><span>Weekly injection or once-daily tablet, subject to prescribing.</span></div><div><strong>Injection</strong><span>Standard escalation begins at 0.25mg weekly; different maximum routes apply to defined groups.</span></div><div><strong>Tablet</strong><span>1.5mg, 4mg, 9mg and 25mg once daily with fasting instructions.</span></div></div></div><div class="qr-block"><nav aria-label="On this page" class="authority-jumps"><strong>On this page</strong><a href="#what-wegovy-is">What Wegovy is</a><a href="#the-weekly-injection-route">The weekly injection route</a><a href="#the-daily-wegovy-pill">The daily Wegovy pill</a><a href="#results-and-expectations">Results and expectations</a><a href="#side-effects-and-muscle-retention">Side effects and muscle retention</a><a href="#access-and-what-happens-next">Access and what happens next</a></nav></div><div class="qr-block"><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what-wegovy-is" aria-hidden="true"></span></div><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-feature"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-1">What Wegovy is</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Wegovy contains semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist used with diet and physical activity for weight management in eligible people. It affects appetite regulation and can help people feel fuller and reduce hunger.</p><p>The injection and tablet contain the same active ingredient but are not interchangeable DIY formats. Their doses, administration and transition instructions differ and require prescriber oversight.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="the-weekly-injection-route" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-2">The weekly injection route</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The injection route normally begins at 0.25mg once weekly and increases gradually. The familiar standard maintenance route reaches 2.4mg weekly. A 7.2mg maximum weekly dose has also been authorised for adult patients with obesity only where clinically indicated after the standard route.</p><p>The MHRA approved a single-dose 7.2mg pen in April 2026. This higher dose does not apply to every person using Wegovy and should never be improvised from assumptions about dose or product availability.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="the-daily-wegovy-pill" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-3">The daily Wegovy pill</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The Wegovy tablet was authorised by the MHRA on 11 June 2026. The starting dose is 1.5mg once daily, increasing through 4mg and 9mg to 25mg, with at least one month at each level.</p><p>Administration matters: the tablet should be swallowed whole after fasting for at least eight hours, with a sip of water (no more than 120 mL), followed by at least 30 minutes before food, drink or other oral medicines. Eating or drinking earlier can reduce absorption. This routine is an important practical difference from Foundayo.</p><p>Taking the tablet? Read our <a href="/articles/oral-semaglutide-for-weight-loss">oral semaglutide guide</a> for the OASIS 4 evidence, fasting routine and first-month plan, then <a href="/compare-weight-loss-treatments#wegovy-pill-vs-foundayo">compare it with Foundayo</a>.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="results-and-expectations" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-4">Results and expectations</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Study averages help compare evidence, but the injection and tablet trials used different populations, designs and timeframes. They should not be presented as a direct head-to-head promise.</p><p>A useful decision weighs likely benefit against side effects, routine, cost, access, adherence and the person's broader plan. The most impressive percentage is useless if the treatment cannot be used safely or consistently.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="shift-depth-wegovy-comparison" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-5">How do I compare Wegovy tablets and injections for my actual week?</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The useful question is not simply “Which format do I prefer?” You and your prescriber need to consider your other medicines, the instructions for the exact product, your routine and the service available to you. The milligram numbers on different formulations are not a do-it-yourself conversion.</p><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table style="width:100%;min-width:480px;border-collapse:collapse;color:inherit;font:inherit;"><caption>Take these questions to the service assessing you</caption><thead style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><tr><th scope="col" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">Question</th><th scope="col" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">Why the answer matters</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">Which exact product and formulation are you considering?</th><td style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">“Semaglutide” or “Wegovy” alone is not a complete set of instructions.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">How would the instructions fit breakfast, shifts and my other oral medicines?</th><td style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">Describe your real morning or waking routine. Ask the pharmacist or prescriber to resolve clashes rather than changing another medicine yourself.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">What should I do if I miss a dose or cannot follow the routine?</th><td style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">Use instructions for the exact formulation. Do not borrow an injection rule for a tablet.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">What assessment and follow-up are included?</th><td style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">A format preference does not settle clinical suitability or who handles side effects.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row" style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">Is it available through this service now, and what is the complete cost?</th><td style="border:1px solid currentColor;padding:12px;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">UK authorisation, an NHS pathway and a provider having supply are different questions. Record the date and what the quote includes.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div><h3>A useful example: the early shift</h3><p>You normally wake, take another prescribed medicine and leave for work with breakfast on the way. Tell the assessing service that sequence. Ask how each candidate formulation would fit it, and what you would do on a changed shift. Do not rearrange an existing prescription to make a new product easier without professional advice.</p><p>If switching is being considered, ask for a written plan covering the exact product, timing and follow-up. Your prescriber should handle the transition; a comparison page is not a switching instruction.</p><p>Read the <a href="/comparisons/medications/wegovy-injection-vs-tablets">existing formulation comparison</a> with the <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102347/smpc">UK tablet product information</a>. For symptoms and help routes, use the <a href="/articles/wegovy-side-effects-timeline">injection side-effects guide</a> only when that is your formulation.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="side-effects-and-muscle-retention" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-6">Side effects and muscle retention</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><strong>Get urgent medical help for severe stomach pain that does not go away, especially if it spreads to your back, with or without vomiting.</strong> This can indicate pancreatitis. Do not wait for a routine review or company reply. A clinician must assess it; if pancreatitis is confirmed, the medicine must not be restarted.</p><p>Sudden loss of vision, including loss of part of your vision, also needs urgent medical assessment.</p><p>Read the instructions for your exact product and discuss side effects with your prescriber or pharmacist: <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/13800/smpc" rel="noopener noreferrer">Wegovy injection product information</a> · <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102347/smpc" rel="noopener noreferrer">Wegovy tablet product information</a>. Safety information checked 3 October 2026.</p><p>Common effects include nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and vomiting. A prescriber should explain what to expect, when to seek advice and how follow-up works.</p><p>Men losing weight should also think about adequate nutrition, <a href="/articles/protein-for-men-weight-management" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">protein</a> and suitable <a href="/guides/exercise-walking-strength-mobility" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">strength</a> activity. Treatment reduces appetite; it does not automatically preserve muscle or build a sustainable routine.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="access-and-what-happens-next" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-7">Access and what happens next</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The pill is authorised in the UK but MHRA authorisation does not automatically create NHS access. NICE and NHS decisions follow separate processes. Private availability and pricing can change and should always be dated and sourced.</p><p>Shift will maintain separate evidence records for the injection and pill so that a change to one route does not silently alter claims about the other.</p><p>Looking for a specific answer? Explore our <a href="/articles/wegovy-side-effects-timeline">Wegovy side-effects guide</a>, <a href="/articles/wegovy-cost-uk">UK cost guide</a> and <a href="/comparisons/medications/wegovy-vs-orlistat">Wegovy versus Orlistat comparison</a>.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="frequently-asked-questions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-8">Frequently asked questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><details><summary>Is Wegovy available as both an injection and a tablet in the UK?</summary><p>Yes. Wegovy contains semaglutide and now has authorised weekly injection and daily tablet routes in the UK, with different doses and administration instructions.</p></details><details><summary>Can Wegovy tablets and injections be swapped directly?</summary><p>No. The formats use different dose schedules and administration rules. Starting, switching or stopping must be managed by an appropriately qualified prescriber.</p></details><details><summary>Does the Wegovy tablet have fasting instructions?</summary><p>Yes. Current UK instructions require an overnight fast, a small amount of water and a further wait before food, drink or other oral medicines.</p></details><section class="authority-next"><h2>Useful next steps</h2><div><a href="/compare-weight-loss-treatments#wegovy-pill-vs-foundayo"><span>Open</span><strong>Wegovy pill versus Foundayo</strong></a><a href="/weight-loss-tablets-for-men"><span>Open</span><strong>Weight-loss tablets for men</strong></a><a href="/articles/stopping-glp1"><span>Open</span><strong>What happens when you stop GLP-1 treatment?</strong></a></div></section></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-9">Sources you can inspect</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/first-glp-1-tablet-for-weight-loss-approved-in-the-uk" rel="noopener noreferrer">MHRA — first GLP-1 tablet approved for weight loss</a></li><li><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/single-dose-72mg-semaglutide-wegovy-pen-approved-to-treat-adult-patients-with-obesity" rel="noopener noreferrer">MHRA — single-dose Wegovy 7.2mg pen</a></li><li><a href="https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246" rel="noopener noreferrer">NICE — overweight and obesity management</a></li></ul><p>Sources support general information, not an individual suitability decision. Matt lost around 4½ stone over about eleven months through changes to eating, movement and prescribed weight-loss treatment after a clinical assessment. This is his personal experience, not a promise of results. He is not a clinician or prescriber. <a href="/about">Read Matt’s full story</a>.</p><p><a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Read Matt’s profile and the Shift research process →</a></p><aside class="authority-safety"><strong>Important</strong><p>This page provides general UK information. Seek urgent medical help for severe or rapidly worsening symptoms.</p></aside></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">11</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-11">Wegovy questions: side effects, costs and everyday support</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Use information for your exact formulation. A guide about the injection must not be treated as instructions for the tablet, or the other way round.</p><ul><li><a href="/articles/wegovy-side-effects-timeline">Wegovy side effects and warning signs</a> — know what to record and when to seek appropriate help.</li><li><a href="/articles/wegovy-cost-uk">Wegovy costs in the UK</a> — read about comparing the whole quote.</li><li><a href="/comparisons/medications/wegovy-injection-vs-tablets">Wegovy injection versus tablets</a> — compare the formulations and their practical differences.</li><li><a href="/articles/nhs-weight-loss-drugs">NHS medicine access</a> — check the relevant pathway and local service.</li><li><a href="/articles/glp-1-and-exercise">Movement during GLP-1 treatment</a> — explore activity and safety questions.</li><li><a href="/articles/stopping-glp1">Support after stopping treatment</a> — prepare for ongoing care and everyday routines.</li></ul><!-- SHIFT_CONTINUITY_WEGOVY_SUPPORT_START --><style data-continuity-links>.continuity-links{box-sizing:border-box;width:min(1160px,calc(100% - 36px));margin:36px auto;padding:28px;border:1px solid #707762;border-radius:12px;background:#050505;color:#e7e3da;font:17px/1.6 Arial,sans-serif}.continuity-links h2{color:#e7e3da;font-size:clamp(1.45rem,3vw,2rem);line-height:1.2}.continuity-links a{color:#e7e3da;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:3px}.continuity-links a:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #e7e3da;outline-offset:4px}.continuity-links p{max-width:850px}.continuity-links li{margin:8px 0}</style></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">12</span><h2 id="rp-wegovy-12">Keep practical support around the prescription</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>My Timber is free to use before, during and after treatment.
