It offers a different daily routine from the <a href="/wegovy" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Wegovy</a> pill, but convenience is only one part of a responsible treatment decision.</p><p class="authority-byline">Written and researched by <a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Matt O’Brien</a>, founder of Shift Some Timber. Evidence reviewed 2026-08-26.</p></div><div class="qr-graphic rest-art" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true"><p class="qr-micro">A clearer next step.</p><div class="rest-rows"><div><span>01</span><strong>Starting Foundayo: the practical questions</strong></div><div><span>02</span><strong>Foundayo UK approval and availability: latest position</strong></div><div><span>03</span><strong>What changed in August 2026</strong></div></div><p>Read the detail. Keep the context.</p></div></section><div class="qr-body sg-copy"><details class="qr-index" data-rp-decoration><summary>On this page <span aria-hidden="true">+</span></summary><nav aria-label="Page sections"><a href="#rp-foundayo-1">Starting Foundayo: the practical questions</a><a href="#foundayo-regulatory-update-20261019">Foundayo UK approval and availability: latest position</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-3">What changed in August 2026</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-4">How Foundayo differs from the Wegovy pill</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-5">Doses, evidence and expectations</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-6">Side effects and assessment</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-7">Price, private availability and NHS access</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-8">Frequently asked questions</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-9">Sources you can inspect</a><a href="#rp-foundayo-10">Who wrote this?</a></nav></details><div class="qr-sections"><div class="qr-block"><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="foundayo-first-month" aria-hidden="true"></span></div><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-1">Starting Foundayo: the practical questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>What did the main weight-management trial find?</h3><p>ATTAIN-1 randomly assigned 3,127 adults with overweight or obesity, without type 2 diabetes, to orforglipron or placebo for 72 weeks. Everyone received diet and activity counselling. In the intention-to-treat results reported in the UK product information, average weight loss was 12.4% in the highest-dose trial group and 0.9% with placebo.</p><p>This is a group average, not a prediction for you or a direct comparison with Wegovy or Mounjaro. Trial dose figures should not be used to choose your prescribed tablet strength. Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea can occur; gastrointestinal effects can sometimes be severe and cause dehydration. Read the urgent warning signs in the linked first-month plan and discuss suitability and tolerability with your prescriber.</p><p>Source: <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102529/smpc">UK Foundayo product information, sections 4.4 and 5.1</a>, updated 14 August 2026; checked 6 October 2026.</p><p><strong>Foundayo has its own instructions.</strong> Do not borrow Wegovy’s fasting rules or missed-dose advice. The UK leaflet permits a daily dose at any time, with or without food. Ask the pharmacist to check your other medicines and supplements; the absence of a fasting window does not mean there are no interactions.</p><p>Choose a daily anchor you can repeat. Before each new prescription, confirm the strength, review plan and total cost with your service. Do not change the dose yourself.</p><p>For a missed dose, follow the Foundayo leaflet: take it when remembered, with no more than one dose in a day and no double dose. If several days were missed or you vomit after taking it, ask the pharmacist before guessing a restart or replacement.</p><p><a href="/articles/oral-semaglutide-for-weight-loss#tablet-first-month">Use the shared first-month plan</a> for food, practical check-ins and urgent warning signs, and <a href="/comparisons/medications/wegovy-injection-vs-tablets#tablets-and-injections-uk">compare the daily routines and costs</a>.</p><p><a href="/member/dashboard?view=app#today">Open My Timber’s Today screen</a> and look for “Your tablet routine”. If these tablets have already been prescribed for you, optional health tracking lets you save a routine, return for a first-week check-in and say whether a practical step helped. You can use routine support when treatment was arranged elsewhere. Saving a check-in does not contact a clinician; nobody monitors it for symptoms. Medicine decisions stay with your prescribing service.</p><p>For everyday support, use <a href="/guides/nutrition-protein-calories-meal-planning">food and meal planning</a> and <a href="/mens-weight-management">manageable movement and starting steps</a>.</p><p>Sources: <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/first-glp-1-tablet-for-weight-loss-approved-in-the-uk">MHRA: Wegovy tablets authorised, 11 June 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-first-in-europe-to-authorise-orforglipron-for-weight-management-and-type-2-diabetes">MHRA: Foundayo authorised, 10 August 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102344/pil">UK Wegovy tablet leaflet, revised June 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102529/pil">UK Foundayo leaflet, revised August 2026</a>.</p><p class="shift-practical-note">Practical section added and its linked sources checked 6 October 2026 by the SHIFT editorial team. These are general examples, not a personal diet, exercise or treatment prescription. Independent clinical review is not claimed.</p><div class="authority-facts"><div><strong>Medicine</strong><span>Orforglipron, branded Foundayo.</span></div><div><strong>UK authorisation</strong><span>MHRA-authorised on 10 August 2026.</span></div><div><strong>Route</strong><span>Prescription-only tablet taken once daily.</span></div><div><strong>Routine</strong><span>May be taken with or without food; follow the supplied product instructions and prescriber advice.</span></div></div><nav aria-label="On this page" class="authority-jumps"><strong>On this page</strong><a href="#what-changed-in-august-2026">What changed in August 2026</a><a href="#how-foundayo-differs-from-the-wegovy-pill">How Foundayo differs from the Wegovy pill</a><a href="#doses-evidence-and-expectations">Doses, evidence and expectations</a><a href="#side-effects-and-assessment">Side effects and assessment</a><a href="#price-private-availability-and-nhs-access">Price, private availability and NHS access</a></nav><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="what-changed-in-august-2026" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="foundayo-regulatory-update-20261019">Foundayo UK approval and availability: latest position</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Foundayo (orforglipron) was authorised in the UK on 10 August 2026. On 15 October 2026, the European Medicines Agency’s committee recommended EU authorisation; its opinion was published on 16 October. This is a separate European regulatory step. It does not confirm NHS funding, stock at a particular pharmacy or supply through SHIFT.</p><p>SHIFT supply is not confirmed. For the practical differences, <a href="/compare-weight-loss-treatments#wegovy-pill-vs-foundayo">compare Foundayo and Wegovy tablets</a>, read our <a href="/weight-loss-tablets-for-men">guide to weight-loss tablets for men</a>, or use the <a href="/articles/oral-semaglutide-for-weight-loss#tablet-first-month">tablet first-month plan</a>.</p><p>Sources: <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-first-in-europe-to-authorise-orforglipron-for-weight-management-and-type-2-diabetes" rel="noopener noreferrer">MHRA, 10 August 2026</a>; <a href="https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/foundayo" rel="noopener noreferrer">EMA opinion adopted 15 October and published 16 October 2026</a>. Regulatory status checked 19 October 2026; this does not renew the review dates of other sections.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-3">What changed in August 2026</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>On 10 August 2026 the MHRA authorised orforglipron, branded Foundayo, for weight management and type 2 diabetes in defined adult populations. The UK became the first country in Europe to authorise it.</p><p>That means older pages describing Foundayo as merely experimental or not UK-authorised are now stale. It does not mean automatic NHS access, universal suitability or that every advertised online product is legitimate.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="how-foundayo-differs-from-the-wegovy-pill" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-4">How Foundayo differs from the Wegovy pill</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Both are daily GLP-1 tablets, but they contain different active ingredients. Wegovy tablets contain semaglutide and require an overnight fast, a small amount of water and a wait before food or drink. Foundayo contains orforglipron and has a more flexible relationship with food and water.</p><p>The easier routine may matter to people who take other morning medicines, work shifts or struggle with fasting instructions. It does not make Foundayo clinically better for every individual.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="doses-evidence-and-expectations" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-5">Doses, evidence and expectations</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Foundayo uses a staged dose-escalation route. The exact current strengths and product instructions must be checked against the authorised UK product information rather than copied from an older trial or another country's label.</p><p>Trial averages can describe what happened across a study population. They cannot predict an individual's result, and separate Foundayo, Wegovy and <a href="/mounjaro" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">Mounjaro</a> trials are not direct head-to-head comparisons.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="side-effects-and-assessment" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-6">Side effects and assessment</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><strong>Get urgent medical help for severe stomach pain that does not go away, especially if it spreads to your back, with or without vomiting.</strong> This can indicate pancreatitis. Do not wait for a routine review or company reply. A clinician must assess it; if pancreatitis is confirmed, the medicine must not be restarted.</p><p>Read the instructions for your exact product and discuss side effects with your prescriber or pharmacist: <a href="https://www.medicines.org.uk/emc/product/102531/smpc" rel="noopener noreferrer">Foundayo UK product information</a>. Safety information checked 3 October 2026.</p><p>Gastrointestinal effects such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation can occur with GLP-1 medicines. Suitability depends on medical history, current medicines, risks and the prescriber's assessment.</p><p>Use a regulated prescribing and pharmacy service. Do not buy products presented as weight-loss medicines through social media, gyms or unregulated sellers.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="price-private-availability-and-nhs-access" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-7">Price, private availability and NHS access</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Private launch prices and provider availability can move rapidly. Any Shift price tracker must display the provider, strength, date checked and what the price includes.</p><p>NHS use requires separate assessment through NICE and implementation decisions. 'MHRA-authorised', 'available privately' and 'available through the NHS' must never be treated as interchangeable statements.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="frequently-asked-questions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="rp-foundayo-8">Frequently asked questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><details><summary>What is Foundayo?</summary><p>Foundayo is the brand name for orforglipron, a prescription-only daily GLP-1 tablet authorised by the MHRA in August 2026 for defined adult populations.</p></details><details><summary>Is Foundayo the same as the Wegovy pill?</summary><p>No. Foundayo contains orforglipron while Wegovy tablets contain semaglutide. An in-depth UK guide to GLP-1 weight-management medicines: how they may help, side effects and drawbacks, costs, implications, alternatives and a proper medication-free route.

UK-focusedEvidence-awareUpdated 8 August 2026Free guide
Quick answer

GLP-1-based medicines can be powerful tools for some people, but they are not the only route and they are not automatically the right route. This guide helps you compare medication with structured lifestyle change, NHS support, professional nutrition help and other options.

In this guideWhat are GLP-1 weight-management medicines? →How could they help? →How could they hinder? →Costs and practical implications →Compare all the main options →What if I want to try without medication first? →Actions before deciding →

What are GLP-1 weight-management medicines?

GLP-1-based medicines mimic or enhance gut-hormone signals involved in appetite, fullness and blood-sugar regulation. Different medicines act on different receptors. Semaglutide acts primarily through GLP-1, while tirzepatide acts through GIP and GLP-1 receptors.

They are prescription medicines, not supplements. They are intended to sit alongside changes to diet and physical activity rather than replacing them.

How could they help?

Appetite

Many people find they feel fuller sooner or think about food less often, which can make a calorie deficit easier to sustain.

Health risk

For suitable people, clinically meaningful weight loss may improve weight-related risk factors and mobility.

Momentum

Early progress can create room to build walking, protein, sleep and other habits that were difficult when appetite felt relentless.

How could they hinder?

Common practical problems include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation and other gastrointestinal effects. Some people struggle to eat enough protein or fluid when appetite falls sharply. There are also costs, monitoring requirements and the question of what happens if treatment is stopped.

Medication can become a poor fit if somebody sees it as the entire plan rather than one tool within a longer-term strategy.

Costs and practical implications

NHS: access depends on the medicine, NICE recommendations, local rollout and individual eligibility. Private: prices vary by provider, medicine and dose and can change. Always check current pricing before committing.

Also budget for the non-financial costs: regular reviews, side-effect management, food planning, treatment administration and a maintenance plan.

What if I want to try without medication first?

A proper medication-free route: the 12-week self-start plan

This is not “just eat less”. It is a structured way to change the environment around your eating, movement and habits so you rely less on willpower.

Weeks 1–2: establish your baseline

  • Record weight and waist once a week, not ten times a day.
  • Use the calorie and protein calculators as rough guides, not commandments.
  • Track a normal week of meals without trying to be perfect.
  • Choose one walking target you can repeat most days.
  • Notice sleep, alcohol, hunger and stress patterns.

Weeks 3–6: make the easy wins boringly repeatable

  • Build meals around protein, vegetables or fruit, and a sensible portion of carbohydrate.
  • Reduce the foods and drinks that add lots of calories without filling you up — but do not ban everything you enjoy.
  • Plan two or three default breakfasts, lunches and evening meals.
  • Increase walking gradually and add basic strength work if appropriate.
  • Design your home and shopping habits so the better option is easier to choose.

Weeks 7–10: deal with real life

  • Plan for takeaways, weekends, football, meals out and holidays instead of pretending they will disappear.
  • Use weekly averages and waist trends rather than reacting to one weigh-in.
  • If hunger is high, review protein, fibre, sleep and the size of your calorie deficit.
  • If progress stalls for several weeks, adjust one thing at a time.

Weeks 11–12: decide what you need next

  • If you are progressing and the plan feels liveable, keep going.
  • If you are trying hard but hunger, health or repeated regain is making progress very difficult, speak to an appropriate healthcare professional about additional options.
  • If you want structure and accountability rather than medication, consider a dietitian, evidence-based Shift Programme or coaching support.

Actions before deciding

  1. Check your current weight, waist and blood pressure.
  2. Review any medical conditions and medicines with an appropriate healthcare professional.
  3. Try a structured lifestyle plan if you have not already done so and it is safe.
  4. If considering medication, use a regulated UK prescriber and pharmacy.
  5. Ask what happens if side effects are difficult, stock changes, or you want to stop.
  6. Have a maintenance plan from day one rather than waiting until the weight has gone.
Shift Says

There is no medal for choosing the hardest route. There is also no failure in trying the free route first. The best option is the one that is safe, evidence-based and realistic enough for you to stick with.

Common questions

Are GLP-1 medicines a shortcut?

They are a treatment tool. They can make appetite management easier, but nutrition, movement, monitoring and maintenance still matter.

Will everybody lose a lot of weight?

No. Average trial results do not predict an individual result, and response varies.

Can I start naturally first?

Yes, if it is safe and appropriate for you. A structured lifestyle attempt can be a sensible first step.

What happens when I stop?

Appetite and weight can change after stopping, which is why maintenance planning and clinical advice matter.

Sources & further reading

We prioritise recognised UK health bodies and primary clinical sources. Guidance can change, so always check the linked source for the latest position.

  • NHS: Overweight and obesity in adults
  • NHS: Tirzepatide
  • NHS: Semaglutide
  • NICE: Tirzepatide for managing overweight and obesity
  • NICE: Overweight and obesity management

Can I do this myself?

Yes. If it is safe for you to do so, use the free plan in this guide, the Knowledge Hub, calculators and trackers before deciding whether you want paid support.

Compare the treatment — not the hype.

Written and researched by Matt O’Brien, founder of Shift Some Timber.

Mounjaro, injectable Wegovy, the new oral Wegovy formulation, liraglutide and Orlistat compared across efficacy evidence, convenience, NHS context, maturity, side-effect burden and maintenance implications.

Updated 8 August 2026UK licensed optionsX vs Y battleEvidence-led
2026 matters here.

Wegovy is no longer just the familiar 2.4 mg weekly injection story. UK product information now includes a 7.2 mg weekly injectable maintenance option for adults with obesity if needed, and a once-daily 25 mg tablet formulation. Comparisons that ignore those changes are already dated.

Treatment Battle

Pick any two licensed options

VS

What the evidence actually tells us

Mounjaro vs injectable Wegovy

SURMOUNT-5 provides a genuine head-to-head anchor: tirzepatide produced greater mean weight loss than semaglutide 1.7/2.4 mg at 72 weeks. That trial does not answer tirzepatide versus the newly licensed 7.2 mg Wegovy dose.

Oral Wegovy

OASIS 4 gives direct phase 3b evidence for oral semaglutide 25 mg: mean weight change was -13.6% at 64 weeks under the treatment-policy analysis.

Liraglutide

Saxenda has a mature obesity evidence base, but average loss is lower than the newer weekly incretin options and it requires daily injections.

Where Ozempic fits

Ozempic contains semaglutide, but it is not the UK weight-management brand/licence. Wegovy is the semaglutide product licensed for obesity/overweight weight management. We include Ozempic only because confusing the two is one of the most common medication questions.

Read the Ozempic clarification guide →

What we deliberately do not do

  • We do not convert trial averages into a promise for an individual.
  • We do not treat a 10/10 rating as a clinical recommendation.
  • We do not pretend NICE recommendation equals immediate NHS availability.
  • We do not publish a fixed private price as though it will still be correct next month.
  • We do not rank Ozempic as a licensed UK obesity-treatment alternative to Wegovy.

The best medication is not simply the one with the biggest trial number.

Route, tolerability, access, cost, diabetes/cardiovascular context, preference for tablets or injections and what happens long term all matter.

This category hub explains the authorised routes, the routines that differ, and why 'prefer not to inject' is a valid practical preference rather than something to be dismissed.</p><p class="authority-byline">Written and researched by <a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Matt O’Brien</a>, founder of Shift Some Timber. Different trials do not establish which treatment will work best for you.</p></div><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-feature"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">01</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-tablets-for-men-1">The current oral market</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The UK now has two authorised daily <a href="/glp1-knowledge-centre" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">GLP-1</a> tablet routes for weight management: semaglutide under the Wegovy brand and orforglipron under the Foundayo brand. Orlistat remains an established non-GLP-1 oral option with a different mechanism and side-effect profile.</p><p>Do not treat 'weight-loss pill' as one medicine category with interchangeable products. The active ingredient, evidence, routine, risks, access and price differ.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="wegovy-pill" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-tablets-for-men-2">Wegovy pill</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The Wegovy pill contains semaglutide. It is taken after an overnight fast with a small amount of water, followed by a wait before food, drink or other medicines. This administration routine is part of how the medicine is used effectively.</p><p>It may suit somebody who prefers tablets and can reliably manage that morning routine. It may be less convenient for others.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="foundayo" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-tablets-for-men-3">Foundayo</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Foundayo contains orforglipron. Its day-to-day advantage is flexibility around food and water compared with oral semaglutide. It is a different molecule with its own dose route, evidence and safety information.</p><p>Convenience, expected benefit, tolerability, other medicines and access all belong in the decision.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="tablets-versus-injections" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-tablets-for-men-4">Tablets versus injections</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>A daily tablet avoids needles, pens and refrigeration, but it creates a daily adherence task. Weekly injections reduce the number of dosing days but require injection technique, storage and sharps disposal.</p><p>Neither route is morally better or more serious. The responsible choice is the authorised treatment a prescriber considers suitable and the person can use consistently.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="how-to-compare-providers" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-tablets-for-men-5">How to compare providers</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Check that prescribing is carried out by an appropriately regulated professional and dispensing by a legitimate UK pharmacy. Compare the full monthly cost, included follow-up, cancellation terms, delivery, dose changes and support rather than a promotional first-month headline.</p><p>Prices and availability are time-sensitive. They are not interchangeable and require individual assessment.</p></details><details><summary>Are tablets weaker than weight-loss injections?</summary><p>Route alone does not determine whether a treatment is appropriate or effective for an individual. More is not automatically better, and copying somebody else's dose is unsafe.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="side-effects-and-when-to-ask-for-help" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-injections-for-men-3">Side effects and when to ask for help</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation are common across these medicines. The treating service should explain expected symptoms, hydration, follow-up and red flags.</p><p>Severe, persistent or worrying symptoms require appropriate medical advice. This site cannot assess an individual or replace their treating service.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="protecting-strength-and-day-to-day-function" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-injections-for-men-4">Protecting strength and day-to-day function</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Rapid weight loss without attention to nutrition and strength can leave a bloke lighter but not necessarily stronger or better able to live his life. Adequate <a href="/articles/protein-for-men-weight-management" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">protein</a>, suitable resistance work, <a href="/articles/walking-for-weight-management-men" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">walking</a>, sleep and recovery deserve a place in the plan.</p><p>The aim is not simply to make the scale move. It is to improve health and help somebody feel more like himself again.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="nhs-and-private-decisions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-injections-for-men-5">NHS and private decisions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>NHS access is governed by recommendations, implementation and local pathways. Private providers apply their own service criteria within prescribing rules. Compare clinical follow-up and overall service quality, not only the cheapest headline.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="frequently-asked-questions" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-injections-for-men-6">Frequently asked questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><details><summary>What are the main UK weight-loss injections?</summary><p>Mounjaro contains tirzepatide and Wegovy contains semaglutide. Both use weekly injection routes but have different mechanisms, doses and evidence.</p></details><details><summary>Do weight-loss injections require dose increases?</summary><p>Both routes normally begin at a lower dose and increase gradually where clinically appropriate. Dose changes must be controlled by the prescriber.</p></details><details><summary>Do injections replace food and exercise planning?</summary><p>No. Nutrition, suitable movement, strength, sleep and follow-up remain important for health, muscle retention and sustainable outcomes.</p></details><section class="authority-next"><h2>Useful next steps</h2><div><a href="/mounjaro"><span>Open</span><strong>Complete Mounjaro hub</strong></a><a href="/wegovy"><span>Open</span><strong>Complete Wegovy hub</strong></a><a href="/compare-weight-loss-treatments#tablets-vs-injections"><span>Open</span><strong>Compare tablets and injections</strong></a></div></section></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="rp-weight-loss-injections-for-men-7">Sources you can inspect</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/mhra-authorises-diabetes-drug-mounjaro-tirzepatide-for-weight-management-and-weight-loss" rel="noopener noreferrer">MHRA — Mounjaro weight-management authorisation</a></li><li><a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/news/single-dose-72mg-semaglutide-wegovy-pen-approved-to-treat-adult-patients-with-obesity" rel="noopener noreferrer">MHRA — Wegovy 7.2mg pen</a></li><li><a href="https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng246" rel="noopener noreferrer">NICE — overweight and obesity management</a></li></ul><p>Sources support general information, not an individual suitability decision. <section class="sp-hero sp-tc2" aria-labelledby="nhh-title-treatment-comparison"><div class="sp-copy"><p class="sp-eyebrow">COMPARE WEIGHT-LOSS TREATMENTS</p><h1 id="nhh-title-treatment-comparison">Weight-loss treatment.<br>Compare the options.</h1><p class="sp-lede">Understand the different routes and their trade-offs without pretending one answer fits every man.</p><div class="sp-actions"><a class="sp-button" href="#mounjaro-vs-wegovy">Compare treatment options<span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a><a class="sp-link" href="#sp-questions">Prepare your questions<span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></div><p class="sp-note">General information. A qualified prescriber decides individual suitability.</p></div><div class="sp-comparison-grid"><aside class="sp-panel" id="sp-questions"><h2>A better-informed conversation</h2><p>These prompts can help you get clear on what matters to you before comparing options.</p><dl><dt>What fits my routine?</dt><dd>Think about how each option might fit with your day-to-day life.</dd><dt>What are the trade-offs?</dt><dd>Consider the potential benefits and downsides for you.</dd><dt>What should I ask?</dt><dd>Use these comparisons to help shape your questions with a prescriber.</dd></dl></aside><nav class="sp-comparison-topics" aria-label="Choose a comparison"><h2>Choose a comparison</h2><p>Explore our guides to understand the key differences and what to think about.</p><a class="sp-step" href="#mounjaro-vs-wegovy"><span><strong>Mounjaro versus Wegovy</strong><span>Compare the key differences to consider.</span></span><span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a><a class="sp-step" href="#wegovy-pill-vs-foundayo"><span><strong>Wegovy pill versus Foundayo</strong><span>Look at how these options differ in practice.</span></span><span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a><a class="sp-step" href="#tablets-vs-injections"><span><strong>Tablets versus injections</strong><span>Explore the pros and cons of each approach.</span></span><span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a><a class="sp-step" href="#medication-versus-surgery"><span><strong>Medication versus surgery</strong><span>Understand the main differences and trade-offs.</span></span><span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a><a class="sp-link" href="#how-this-comparison-is-governed">How this comparison is governed<span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a></nav></div></section><section class="nhh-context" data-nhh-retained-context aria-label="Page context and existing actions"><p class="authority-standfirst">This centre compares authorised routes and their practical differences. It does not diagnose, prescribe or decide suitability. Evidence records control the facts; a qualified prescriber controls the individual medicine decision.</p><p class="authority-byline">Written and researched by <a href="/authors/matt-obrien">Matt O’Brien</a>, founder of Shift Some Timber. Evidence reviewed 2026-08-26.</p></section>

<section class="authority-section" id="mounjaro-vs-wegovy"><h2>Mounjaro versus Wegovy</h2><p>Mounjaro is weekly tirzepatide; Wegovy injection is weekly semaglutide. They target overlapping but not identical pathways and use different dose schedules. Head-to-head and separate trial evidence should be reported with population, duration and dose context.</p><p>The practical comparison includes response, side effects, dose route, availability, total service cost and whether the surrounding food, movement and follow-up plan is realistic.</p></section><section class="authority-section" id="wegovy-pill-vs-foundayo"><h2>Wegovy pill versus Foundayo</h2><p>Both are daily <a href="/glp1-knowledge-centre" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">GLP-1</a> tablets. Wegovy contains semaglutide and requires an overnight fast plus a wait before food or drink. Foundayo contains orforglipron and has greater flexibility around meals and water.</p><p>Separate trials do not create a direct winner. Routine, tolerability, medical history, expected benefit, cost and availability all require context.</p></section><section class="authority-section" id="tablets-vs-injections"><h2>Tablets versus injections</h2><p>Tablets remove needles and refrigeration but require daily adherence; the Wegovy pill also creates a structured fasting routine. Weekly injections reduce dosing frequency but require storage, injection technique and sharps disposal.</p><p>Preference matters because a treatment that fits real life may be easier to use consistently. Preference cannot override safety or prescribing suitability.</p></section><section class="authority-section" id="medication-versus-surgery"><h2>Medication versus surgery</h2><p>Medicines and bariatric procedures have different eligibility, evidence, reversibility, follow-up and risk profiles. Surgery is not a 'failure' and medicine is not 'cheating'. Both require informed decisions and long-term support.</p><p>People considering surgery need a specialist pathway, provider checks and a clear aftercare plan.</p></section><section class="authority-section" id="how-this-comparison-is-governed"><h2>How this comparison is governed</h2><p>Every medicine record must store its evidence source, UK authorisation status, evidence-review date and affected claims. If a dynamic fact cannot be verified, it should be withdrawn rather than guessed.</p><p>The interactive comparison workspace lets users choose two hero medicines and compare format, starting route, BMI context, evidence, downsides, live HQ price and supply. It remains decision support—not a recommendation or suitability result.</p></section>
<section class="authority-section authority-faq" id="frequently-asked-questions"><h2>Frequently asked questions</h2><details><summary>Which weight-loss treatment is best?</summary><p>There is no universal best treatment. Suitability depends on health, evidence, risks, route, routine, access and an individual assessment by an appropriately qualified professional.</p></details><details><summary>Can separate trial percentages be compared directly?</summary><p>Not reliably without context. Trials may use different populations, doses, durations and methods, so headline percentages should not be treated as a guaranteed league table.</p></details><details><summary>Does this comparison prescribe or recommend treatment?</summary><p>No. It provides general decision support. A qualified prescriber or specialist service remains responsible for an individual treatment decision.</p></details></section>

questions before chasing a prescription</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><ul><li><strong>Is it clinically appropriate?</strong> The prescriber assesses the actual medicine, indication, history and risks.</li><li><strong>Is that use funded through this NHS pathway?</strong> A licensed use is not automatically funded for everyone who meets the licence.</li><li><strong>Which local service provides it?</strong> The answer may be a commissioned primary-care service or a specialist team, not necessarily your own practice.</li></ul><p>NHS England distinguishes specialist eligibility from phased primary-care access and permits different local delivery models. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: NHS England commissioning guidance">[1]</a></p><span id="nhs-mounjaro-eligibility-bmi"></span><span id="rollout"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">02</span><h2 id="mounjaro"><span id="heading-mounjaro">Mounjaro in England: what changed in June 2026?</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>From <strong>23 June 2026</strong>, the primary-care rollout includes the second priority cohort as well as the first. NHS Cheshire and Merseyside describes the threshold as BMI at least 35 with at least four of five specified conditions, with lower BMI thresholds for named ethnic backgrounds. This is not simply “BMI 35 plus any four diagnoses”. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside phased access">[2]</a></p><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table><caption>England: primary-care tirzepatide rollout, as at 19 September 2026</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Phase</th><th scope="col">BMI before ethnicity adjustment</th><th scope="col">Qualifying conditions</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Cohort I—continues</th><td>40 or more</td><td>At least four of the five named conditions</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Cohort II—from 23 June 2026</th><td>35–39.9</td><td>At least four of the five named conditions</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Cohort III—scheduled from 1 April 2027, not yet the current phase</th><td>40 or more</td><td>Three of the five named conditions</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>The five are hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, cardiovascular disease within the commissioning definition, and type 2 diabetes. The clinical definitions matter: for example, the sleep-apnoea criterion is not merely snoring. A clinician checks the diagnoses and applicable treatment criteria. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: NHS England qualifying conditions">[1]</a></p><p>The stated BMI thresholds are usually reduced by 2.5 for South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African and African-Caribbean backgrounds. Ask the service to confirm how the adjustment applies to you. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-2" aria-label="Source 2: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside BMI adjustments">[2]</a></p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">03</span><h2 id="primary"><span id="heading-primary">Specialist access is not the same as the primary-care phase</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>The wider specialist tirzepatide population described by NHS England has BMI at least 35 plus at least one weight-related condition, with the specified ethnicity adjustment and prescribing assessment. Services can prioritise referrals according to clinical need and capacity. Missing the current primary-care cohort therefore does not, by itself, answer whether a specialist referral is appropriate. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: NHS England specialist implementation">[1]</a></p><p>Ask which pathway was considered, who accepts the referral and what happens while you wait. A funding rule is not a promise of an immediate appointment or a particular medicine.</p></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">04</span><h2 id="map"><span id="heading-map">The medicine name alone does not identify the pathway</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><span id="wegovy"></span><strong>Semaglutide (Wegovy):</strong> obesity prescribing through specialist weight-management services has its own criteria. There is also a distinct cardiovascular-risk indication for some people with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. Do not use the Mounjaro obesity cohort table to decide eligibility for that separate indication; ask the GP or cardiac team about the currently commissioned route. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-3" aria-label="Source 3: NHS England weight-management injections">[3]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-4" aria-label="Source 4: NHS semaglutide information">[4]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-5" aria-label="Source 5: NHS regional cardiovascular pathway implementation">[5]</a></p><p><span id="saxenda"></span><strong>Liraglutide (Saxenda):</strong> NHS weight-loss access is through specialist services and is not a routine promise of a GP prescription. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-6" aria-label="Source 6: NHS liraglutide information">[6]</a></p><p><span id="orlistat"></span><strong>Orlistat:</strong> a different, meal-related medicine, available on prescription and in lower-dose pharmacy products. Discuss whether it fits your history and daily routine rather than treating it as an interchangeable injection substitute. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-7" aria-label="Source 7: NHS orlistat information">[7]</a></p><p><span id="diabetes"></span><strong>Type 2 diabetes:</strong> tirzepatide prescribed for blood-glucose management has a separate eligibility pathway from tirzepatide for obesity. Ask which indication is being assessed. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-1" aria-label="Source 1: NHS England distinction between diabetes and obesity pathways">[1]</a></p></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">05</span><h2 id="uk-nations"><span id="heading-uk-nations">Outside England: use your own nation’s route</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>England’s phased table must not be presented as a UK-wide entitlement. Wales has a separate clinical pathway and health-board arrangements. Northern Ireland announced a first-phase obesity management service on 29 June 2026, with implementation expected in early autumn; an announcement is not evidence that every local referral route is already open. <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-8" aria-label="Source 8: Welsh Government clinical pathway">[8]</a> <a class="fa-cite" href="#source-9" aria-label="Source 9: Northern Ireland service announcement">[9]</a></p><p>In Scotland, ask your GP or NHS board which current weight-management service and formulary apply. In Wales, contact your health board; in Northern Ireland, your GP or HSC trust. Get the local route in writing when national headlines and practice information do not seem to match.</p><span id="icb"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">06</span><h2 id="refused"><span id="heading-refused">“Not available” can mean three very different things</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p class="lg-table-hint" data-rp-decoration>Swipe sideways to compare every column.</p><div class="qa-scroll-table-v2224"><table><caption>Ask what the actual barrier is</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Answer you receive</th><th scope="col">Useful follow-up</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Not clinically suitable</th><td>What makes it unsuitable, and what alternatives address the same health need?</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Outside the current funded cohort</th><td>Which indication and care setting were assessed? Is a specialist referral appropriate?</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Local pathway or capacity restriction</th><td>Who commissions the service, how are referrals handled and how can I check for a change?</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>A clear explanation is more useful than repeatedly asking for the same brand. Request the local integrated care board’s pathway in England, or your national/local equivalent elsewhere. Keep the response and any referral details.</p><span id="referral"></span><span id="bloods"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">07</span><h2 id="questions"><span id="heading-questions">A practical appointment checklist—not a self-diagnosis finder</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p><span id="finder"></span><span id="print"></span>Bring your current medicines, known diagnoses, previous weight-management support, any private treatment and the dates of relevant reviews. You do not need to invent a perfect history or start a medicine privately to justify asking for help.</p><ul><li>Which clinical indication and NHS pathway are relevant to me?</li><li>Am I being assessed against primary-care prioritisation or specialist referral criteria?</li><li>What eating, activity and behavioural support comes with treatment?</li><li>What happens if I am unsuitable, outside the current cohort or waiting for capacity?</li><li>Who is responsible for monitoring, side effects and the next review?</li></ul></div></section><section class="qr-section"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">08</span><h2 id="support"><span id="heading-support">Support, waiting and private-to-NHS handover</span></h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><p>Ask for the support available now, not just the prescription you hope might follow. Keep <a href="/mens-mental-health" data-seo-context-link="2026-10-06">mental health</a>, sleep, eating difficulties and mobility in the conversation. A treatment decision should not reduce the appointment to a single BMI number.</p><p><span id="private"></span>Do not assume an NHS service will take over a privately started medicine, match its dose or refund its cost. Ask the receiving service before making financial or treatment plans. Share the exact product and treatment history; leave any switch to the prescribing team.</p><p><span id="shift"></span>My Timber can hold your own goals and treatment/provider history so you do not have to reconstruct them for each conversation. It cannot verify NHS eligibility, advance a waiting list or replace the NHS service’s records. <a href="/member/dashboard?passport=1#journey">Open My Timber</a> · <a href="/programme">Use the Programme’s everyday support</a>.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="faq" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide"><div class="qr-section-title"><span class="qr-section-no" data-rp-decoration aria-hidden="true">09</span><h2 id="fa-faq-heading">Common questions</h2></div><div class="qr-section-detail"><h3>Can my GP prescribe Mounjaro for weight loss now?</h3><p>In England, prescribing depends on clinical assessment and the currently commissioned primary-care or specialist route. The June 2026 rollout is not access for everyone who meets the medicine licence.</p><h3>Does one weight-related condition qualify me?</h3><p>It is not enough for the current England primary-care priority cohorts described here. The specialist pathway has different criteria; ask which setting is appropriate rather than treating the primary-care table as the only route.</p><h3>Can I use the same criteria in Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland?</h3><p>No. The detailed phased table on this page describes England. Confirm your own nation’s and local service’s arrangements.</p><span class="rp-source-anchor" id="sources" aria-hidden="true"></span></div></section><section class="qr-section qr-wide qr-sources"><div
